exercises.name: Opening Chest
exercises.description: Open your arms wide, then bring your palms together as your upper back gently rounds. Alternating these shapes helps you explore chest openness and upper back movement without leaving your chair.
steps: Sit tall on your chair, feet flat and hands on thighs.
Inhale and spread your arms comfortably wide, turning your palms forward.
Exhale and bring your palms together in front of your chest.
Allow your upper back to round slightly as your hands meet.
Continue opening and closing slowly, letting your breath guide each movement.
exercises.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to close
exercises.cue: Open like a pair of curtains
exercises.tip: Keep your arms below shoulder height if a wider opening feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Painting a Rainbow
exercises.description: Trace a curved arc overhead with one arm, then change sides with a small seated weight shift. This flowing reach explores shoulder range and side body length while practicing controlled shifts in balance.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with feet wide and firmly planted.
Lift one arm into a soft curve above your head.
Reach gently across, shifting slightly toward the opposite hip without lifting either foot.
Lower your arm and return your weight to the middle.
Alternate arms slowly, breathing easily through each curved reach.
exercises.breath: Breathe easily through each flowing arc
exercises.cue: Paint a wide ribbon of color
exercises.tip: Keep both sitting bones on the chair and make the overhead arc smaller as needed.

exercises.name: Pulse on the Qi
exercises.description: Hold your palms facing each other and gently widen and narrow the space between them. This small, steady movement encourages relaxed shoulders and gives your attention a clear anchor for following your breath.
steps: Sit upright on your chair with feet resting flat.
Hold your palms facing each other, a few inches apart.
Relax your elbows downward and inhale as your hands separate slightly.
Exhale and bring your palms closer without letting them touch.
Continue this small pulse slowly, keeping your shoulders soft.
exercises.breath: Inhale apart, exhale gently together
exercises.cue: Hold a soft cloud between palms
exercises.tip: Keep your hands near your belly if holding them higher tires your shoulders.

exercises.name: Tao Yin Spinal Twist
exercises.description: You lengthen the spine on an inhale and turn deeply to each side on the exhale, one hand on the opposite knee. It frees the back and leaves you standing taller when you get up.
steps: Sit tall near the front of your chair, hands on your knees.
Inhale and lengthen up through the crown of your head.
Exhale and turn your chest, shoulders and head to the right.
Rest your left hand on your right knee, then return to centre.
Repeat the twist to the left, slow and deep.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to turn
exercises.cue: Grow tall, then turn like a spiral stair
exercises.tip: Lengthen first, then turn; never twist while slumping.

exercises.name: Waving Your Hands to the Sea
exercises.description: Float your hands to chest height and sweep them gently from one side to the other. This seated wave encourages smooth shoulder movement and coordinated arm control while keeping your breathing easy.
steps: Sit upright on your chair with both feet comfortably grounded.
Float both hands forward to chest height, keeping your elbows soft.
Sweep your hands gently toward one side without lifting your shoulders.
Guide your hands back across your body toward the other side.
Continue waving side to side, breathing smoothly without holding your breath.
exercises.breath: Breathe steadily as your hands sweep
exercises.cue: Let your hands ride a wave
exercises.tip: Lower your hands below chest height if your shoulders begin to feel tired.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction Left
exercises.description: Slide your left foot outward from a steady seated position, then draw it back with control. This sideways movement engages your outer hip and practices leg control while your torso stays centered.
steps: Sit near your chair's front with feet flat and spine tall.
Rest your hands on the seat and gently steady your belly.
Slide your left foot sideways, keeping your knee aligned over your foot.
Draw your left foot back beneath your knee without leaning sideways.
Repeat slowly, exhaling outward and inhaling as your foot returns.
exercises.breath: Exhale outward, inhale back to center
exercises.cue: Keep your torso quiet and tall
exercises.tip: Use a smaller sideways slide if your pelvis shifts or your knee feels strained.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction Right
exercises.description: Sit tall and guide your right foot sideways, opening your leg while keeping your torso quiet. This gentle outward movement builds hip control for stepping sideways and changing direction.
steps: Sit near the chair’s front edge with both feet grounded.
Slide your right foot sideways, keeping your knee aligned over your toes.
Bring your right foot back beneath your knee with control.
Repeat slowly, breathing evenly and keeping your shoulders relaxed.
exercises.breath: Exhale outward, inhale back to center
exercises.cue: Keep your torso quietly anchored
exercises.tip: Keep the movement small enough that both sitting bones stay evenly supported.

exercises.name: Bicep Curl
exercises.description: From your chair, bend your elbows to bring your palms toward your shoulders, then lower slowly. This controlled curl engages your upper arms and practices the bending action used when lifting everyday objects.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with arms resting beside your body.
Turn your palms forward and keep your elbows close.
Bend your elbows, bringing your hands toward your shoulders.
Lower your hands slowly, exhaling with each curl and inhaling down.
exercises.breath: Exhale to curl, inhale to lower
exercises.cue: Keep your elbows softly anchored
exercises.tip: Keep your wrists straight and shoulders relaxed rather than squeezing at the top.

exercises.name: Knee Extensions Dynamic
exercises.description: Straighten one knee to lift your foot forward, then lower it smoothly and change legs. This gentle seated rhythm works your front thighs and practices controlled movement through your knees.
steps: Sit upright on a sturdy chair with feet flat.
Straighten your left knee, reaching your heel forward comfortably.
Bend your left knee and lower your foot with control.
Extend and lower your right leg in the same way.
Alternate legs smoothly, exhaling as you extend each knee.
exercises.breath: Exhale to extend, inhale to lower
exercises.cue: Move as smoothly as a slow pendulum
exercises.tip: Keep your thighs resting on the seat and avoid swinging your feet.

exercises.name: Neck Extension Look Up
exercises.description: Sit tall and gently lift your chin to look slightly upward, then return your gaze ahead. This explores comfortable neck extension and builds awareness of moving your head without lifting your shoulders.
steps: Sit tall on a chair with feet flat and shoulders relaxed.
Slowly lift your chin and direct your gaze slightly upward.
Pause briefly within a comfortable range, keeping your shoulders still.
Return your gaze forward slowly and repeat with easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Breathe easily as your gaze rises
exercises.cue: Let your gaze rise like sunrise
exercises.tip: Keep the upward tilt small, and stop if you feel dizziness or discomfort.

exercises.name: Neck Flexion
exercises.description: From a tall seat, gently lower your chin toward your chest while keeping your shoulders relaxed. This gives the back of your neck a mild stretch and encourages controlled head movement.
steps: Sit upright on a chair with feet flat and arms resting.
Slowly lower your chin toward your chest without rounding your back.
Pause where you feel a gentle stretch behind your neck.
Lift your head back to level and repeat slowly.
exercises.breath: Exhale to lower, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Let your chin nod toward your heart
exercises.tip: Let your head move without pulling it down or forcing your chin to touch your chest.

exercises.name: Neck Side Bend Ear to Shoulder
exercises.description: Sit tall and gently tip one ear toward your shoulder, keeping both shoulders relaxed. This small sideways stretch helps you explore neck mobility without turning your head.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with both feet resting flat.
Keep your face forward as you tip one ear sideways.
Let the opposite shoulder stay heavy without pulling your head.
Return to center slowly, then alternate sides with easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Breathe slowly, soften with each exhale
exercises.cue: Let your ear drift toward your shoulder
exercises.tip: Keep the tilt small and comfortable, stopping if you notice dizziness or discomfort.

exercises.name: Seated Row Upper Back Squeeze
exercises.description: Reach your arms forward, then draw your elbows back beside your ribs with a gentle shoulder blade squeeze. This rowing motion engages your upper back and improves shoulder blade control.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with feet flat and chest relaxed.
Reach both arms forward with palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows and draw them back beside your ribs.
Bring your shoulder blades gently together without lifting your shoulders.
Reach forward again, repeating slowly with an exhale as you pull.
exercises.breath: Exhale to pull, inhale to reach
exercises.cue: Slide your elbows into back pockets
exercises.tip: Keep your ribs over your hips rather than arching your back as you pull.

exercises.name: Shoulder Extension
exercises.description: Sweep your arms a little behind your hips as you sit tall, bringing your shoulder blades gently together. This backward reach develops shoulder mobility for movements like reaching behind you.
steps: Sit on your chair with feet flat and arms beside you.
Lengthen your arms downward, keeping your elbows soft.
Move both arms slightly backward without leaning your chest forward.
Draw your shoulder blades gently together and keep your neck relaxed.
Return your arms beside you, repeating slowly with easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Exhale back, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Reach your fingertips behind your hips
exercises.tip: Keep the reach small, and avoid pushing your ribs forward to move farther.

exercises.name: Shoulder Rolls
exercises.description: Circle your shoulders slowly up, forward, and down, then reverse the direction while your arms hang loosely. These gentle circles explore shoulder mobility and encourage you to release unnecessary tension.
steps: Sit comfortably on your chair with spine tall and arms relaxed.
Lift your shoulders gently toward your ears as you inhale.
Roll your shoulders forward and down as you exhale.
Repeat several smooth circles, letting your arms hang loosely.
Reverse direction, rolling up, back, and down with slow breaths.
exercises.breath: Inhale up, exhale around and down
exercises.cue: Draw soft circles with your shoulders
exercises.tip: Make smaller circles if needed, and let your head stay centered over your chest.

exercises.name: Seated Mountain Pose
exercises.description: Sit tall with your feet grounded and your hands resting lightly on your thighs. This quiet posture helps you practice upright alignment while giving your ribs room to move with each breath.
steps: Sit on your chair with both feet flat on the floor.
Rest your hands on your thighs and lengthen through your crown.
Let your shoulders settle down while keeping your chest gently lifted.
Stay tall and breathe comfortably, softening your face with each exhale.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to settle
exercises.cue: Grow tall from grounded roots
exercises.tip: Place a firm support beneath your feet if they do not reach the floor.

exercises.name: Seated Chest Opener
exercises.description: Open your arms wide at shoulder height as you sit upright with grounded feet. This position gently stretches the front of your chest and helps you practice opening without arching your lower back.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with both feet flat on the floor.
Raise your arms out to the sides, reaching gently through your fingertips.
Soften your elbows and let your shoulders drop away from your ears.
Hold comfortably as you breathe, then lower your arms slowly.
exercises.breath: Inhale across your chest, exhale softly
exercises.cue: Open your arms like wide curtains
exercises.tip: Keep your arms below shoulder height if lifting them higher feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Seated Cat Cow Stretches
exercises.description: Gently lift your chest, then round your back with your hands supported on your thighs. This flowing movement explores spinal flexibility and helps you coordinate changes in posture with your breath.
steps: Sit on your chair with feet flat and hands on your thighs.
Inhale and tip your pelvis forward slightly, lifting your chest gently.
Exhale and tip your pelvis back, rounding your spine and lowering your chin.
Flow between lifting and rounding, letting each breath guide your pace.
exercises.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to round
exercises.cue: Let your spine ripple gently
exercises.tip: Keep the movement small and comfortable, especially if your back feels sensitive.

exercises.name: Seated Side Bend Left
exercises.description: Reach your left arm overhead and lean gently right, keeping both hips grounded on your chair. This stretch lengthens your left side and explores sideways movement through your ribs and waist.
steps: Sit on your chair with feet flat and both hips evenly grounded.
Rest your right hand on the seat and lift your left arm overhead.
Lean gently right, reaching your left fingertips upward and across.
Breathe into your left ribs, then slowly return upright and lower your arm.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale into the bend
exercises.cue: Make space along your left waist
exercises.tip: Keep your left hip heavy, and bend your raised elbow if your shoulder feels strained.

exercises.name: Seated Side Bend Right
exercises.description: Reach your right arm overhead and lean gently left, keeping both hips grounded on your chair. This stretch lengthens your right side and explores sideways movement through your ribs and waist.
steps: Sit on your chair with feet flat and both hips evenly grounded.
Rest your left hand on the seat and lift your right arm overhead.
Lean gently left, reaching your right fingertips upward and across.
Breathe into your right ribs, then slowly return upright and lower your arm.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale into the bend
exercises.cue: Make space along your right waist
exercises.tip: Keep your right hip heavy, and bend your raised elbow if your shoulder feels strained.

exercises.name: Seated Savasana
exercises.description: Rest against your chair with your feet supported and your hands loose on your thighs. This seated pause gives you time to notice your breathing and let go of effort after movement.
steps: Sit with your back supported by the chair and feet resting flat.
Let your hands rest on your thighs and soften your shoulders.
Close your eyes if comfortable, or rest your gaze downward.
Allow your breath to settle naturally as you rest quietly.
exercises.breath: Let each breath come and go
exercises.cue: Let the chair carry your weight
exercises.tip: Keep your eyes open if closing them makes you feel unsteady or uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch Left
exercises.description: Extend your left heel forward from your chair and tip your torso gently over your leg. This lengthens the back of your thigh and practices folding from your hips with a long spine.
steps: Sit near the front of your chair with feet grounded.
Extend your left leg forward, resting your heel and lifting your toes.
Rest your hands on your thighs and lengthen your spine.
Tip forward from your hips until your left thigh feels a stretch.
Hold your comfortable position, breathing slowly without reaching farther.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to hinge
exercises.cue: Fold from your hips like a hinge
exercises.tip: Keep a small bend in your left knee rather than forcing it straight.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch Right
exercises.description: Place your right heel ahead of your chair and lean forward from your hips, keeping your back long. This stretches your right hamstring and builds awareness of hip movement without rounding your spine.
steps: Sit near the front of your chair with feet grounded.
Reach your right heel forward, keeping your toes pointed upward.
Place your hands on your thighs and sit a little taller.
Hinge gently forward from your hips, keeping your chest open.
Pause at a mild stretch and take slow, easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to soften
exercises.cue: Reach your chest forward, not down
exercises.tip: Stop your forward lean before your back rounds or your knee feels strained.

exercises.name: Seated Side Crunches Left
exercises.description: Bend gently to your left, bringing your left ribs toward your hip while your right hand supports you. This works the muscles along your waist and develops control during sideways trunk movement.
steps: Sit tall on a sturdy chair with both feet flat.
Hold the seat with your right hand for steady support.
Place your left fingertips behind your ear, keeping your neck long.
Exhale and bend left, drawing your left ribs toward your hip.
Inhale to return upright, then repeat with a small, smooth bend.
exercises.breath: Exhale to bend, inhale to rise
exercises.cue: Shorten the space along your waist
exercises.tip: Keep both sitting bones on the seat and avoid pulling on your head.

exercises.name: Seated Side Crunches Right
exercises.description: Draw your right ribs toward your right hip in a small seated side bend, using your left hand for support. This strengthens your side waist and practices returning upright with smooth, deliberate control.
steps: Sit tall on a sturdy chair with both feet flat.
Place your left hand on the seat to support your balance.
Rest your right fingertips behind your ear without pulling your head.
Exhale and bend right, bringing your right ribs toward your hip.
Inhale as you sit tall, then repeat the gentle sideways movement.
exercises.breath: Exhale to bend, inhale to rise
exercises.cue: Bring your ribs toward your pocket
exercises.tip: Keep your chest facing forward so the movement stays sideways rather than twisting.

exercises.name: Seated Knee to Elbow Crunches
exercises.description: From your chair, lift one knee and turn your opposite elbow toward it with a small curl through your torso. This crossing pattern builds abdominal control and coordination between your upper and lower body.
steps: Sit near the front of a sturdy chair, feet planted comfortably.
Rest your fingertips behind your ears, keeping your elbows comfortably wide.
Lift your right knee and curl your left elbow toward it.
Lower your foot and sit tall before switching sides.
Alternate slowly, exhaling with each curl and inhaling as you return.
exercises.breath: Exhale to curl, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Fold gently across your middle
exercises.tip: Keep your hands light and let your elbow and knee stay apart.

exercises.name: Seated Marching
exercises.description: Lift and lower your knees one at a time, making a quiet, steady march from your chair. This alternating movement strengthens your hip flexors and practices leg coordination while your trunk stays stable.
steps: Sit near the chair front with feet flat and hip-width apart.
Hold the chair sides lightly and lengthen through your spine.
Lift your right knee a comfortable distance, keeping it bent.
Lower your right foot softly, then lift your left knee.
Continue alternating at an easy rhythm while breathing evenly.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly with your marching rhythm
exercises.cue: Make each footfall soft and quiet
exercises.tip: Keep each lift small enough that you can stay upright without rocking backward.

exercises.name: Seated Warrior II Left
exercises.description: Open your left knee outward and extend your arms in opposite directions while your chair supports you. This steady shape builds shoulder endurance and explores a wider range through your hips.
steps: Sit near the front of a sturdy, armless chair, feet grounded.
Open your left knee leftward, aligning it over your left ankle.
Extend your right leg diagonally right, keeping your foot firmly grounded.
Reach both arms sideways at shoulder height, palms facing down.
Look over your left hand and hold with smooth, easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Breathe steadily across your open chest
exercises.cue: Reach toward two distant horizons
exercises.tip: Keep your seat supported, and lower your arms whenever your shoulders need a break.

exercises.name: Seated Warrior II Right
exercises.description: Open your right knee outward and extend your arms in opposite directions while your chair supports you. This steady shape builds shoulder endurance and explores a wider range through your hips.
steps: Sit near the front of a sturdy, armless chair, feet grounded.
Open your right knee rightward, aligning it over your right ankle.
Extend your left leg diagonally left, keeping your foot firmly grounded.
Reach both arms sideways at shoulder height, palms facing down.
Look over your right hand and hold with smooth, easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Breathe steadily across your open chest
exercises.cue: Reach toward two distant horizons
exercises.tip: Keep your seat supported, and lower your arms whenever your shoulders need a break.

exercises.name: Full Body Breathing
exercises.description: Cradle an imaginary ball near your belly, slowly widening your hands as you inhale and drawing them closer as you exhale. This quiet standing practice links steady posture with relaxed, coordinated breathing.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft and shoulders relaxed.
Curve your hands before your lower belly, palms facing each other.
Inhale gently as you open your hands a little wider.
Exhale slowly as your hands float back toward each other.
Repeat at your natural breathing pace, keeping your feet evenly grounded.
exercises.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to gather
exercises.cue: Let a soft balloon expand
exercises.tip: Keep the hand movement small enough that your shoulders stay relaxed and your breathing feels easy.

exercises.name: Full Body Shaking
exercises.description: Bounce softly from the knees and let the rhythm shake loose through your shoulders, arms and hands. It wakes the whole body in seconds and lets go of the stiffness you carried in.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Start a relaxed bounce from the knees, heels staying down.
Let the bounce travel up and shake your shoulders and arms.
Keep your hands loose, like shaking water from your fingers.
Keep the rhythm going, then slow down and settle into stillness.
exercises.breath: Breathe freely, never hold the breath
exercises.cue: Shake the stiffness out through your fingertips
exercises.tip: Keep the heels grounded and the face soft; the bounce comes from the knees, not the back.

exercises.name: Hip Circles
exercises.description: Hands on your hips, you draw wide, smooth circles with your pelvis while your shoulders stay level. It loosens the hips and lower back so every step and stance that follows feels freer.
steps: Stand with feet a little wider than your hips, hands on hips.
Soften your knees and keep your chest tall.
Circle your hips forward, to the left, back and to the right.
Make the circles wide and smooth, then reverse the direction.
Keep breathing slowly and let your shoulders stay level.
exercises.breath: Breathe slowly and evenly
exercises.cue: Draw a big circle with your belt
exercises.tip: Move the pelvis, not the head; your shoulders stay quietly above your feet.

exercises.name: Back Tapping
exercises.description: You swing your arms behind you and tap the lower back on both sides of the spine with loose fists. It warms the lower back and lets the shoulders and waist relax into a free swing.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Make loose fists and swing both arms behind you.
Tap your lower back on both sides of the spine.
Let the swing come from your waist, light and steady.
Keep tapping softly, then let your arms swing to rest.
exercises.breath: Breathe slowly, exhale as you tap
exercises.cue: Knock gently on the door of your back
exercises.tip: Tap the muscles beside the spine, never the spine itself, and keep it featherlight.

exercises.name: Thigh Tapping
exercises.description: With loose, cupped hands you tap briskly down the fronts and then the outsides of your thighs. The quick rhythm wakes up the legs and warms the big muscles you stand on.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Cup your hands loosely and tap the fronts of your thighs.
Travel down toward the knees and back up to the hips.
Now tap the outsides of your thighs the same way.
Keep the taps light and quick, then let your arms rest.
exercises.breath: Breathe naturally with the rhythm
exercises.cue: Drum lightly on your legs
exercises.tip: Keep the wrists loose so the taps stay light and springy, never hard.

exercises.name: Lung Opening Push & Pull
exercises.description: Reach your interlaced hands forward as your upper back rounds, then draw them toward your chest. This flowing exchange moves your shoulder blades and pairs rib movement with comfortable breathing.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and shoulders relaxed.
Interlace your fingers loosely in front of your chest.
Exhale and reach forward, gently rounding your upper back.
Inhale and draw your hands inward, lifting your breastbone slightly.
Repeat slowly, matching each reach and return to your breath.
exercises.breath: Exhale to reach, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Open like a gentle accordion
exercises.tip: Keep the movement in your upper back rather than arching your lower back.

exercises.name: Qi Ball
exercises.description: Cup your hands around an imaginary ball, gently compressing, rolling, and lifting it in front of you. These small, deliberate movements build hand coordination and help you maintain a quiet, balanced stance.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees softly bent.
Curve your hands around an imaginary ball before your belly.
Bring your palms slightly closer, then ease them apart three times.
Roll your hands clockwise, pulse gently, then reverse and pulse again.
Float the ball up and down your midline, breathing evenly.
exercises.breath: Keep your breath quiet and even
exercises.cue: Hold a light, floating sphere
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows softly bent and your hands below shoulder height.

exercises.name: Qi Clearing
exercises.description: Extend your arms outward and gently turn from side to side, rotating one palm upward with each turn. This loose, rhythmic movement practices coordinated turning while keeping your shoulders easy.
steps: Stand slightly wider than shoulder-width with your knees softly bent.
Open your arms to the sides at a comfortable height.
Turn your hips and chest left, rotating your right palm upward.
Return through center, then turn right with your left palm upward.
Continue alternating, inhaling toward center and exhaling with each turn.
exercises.breath: Inhale to center, exhale to turn
exercises.cue: Let your arms follow the breeze
exercises.tip: Keep turns small, allowing your heels to pivot so your knees stay comfortable.

exercises.name: Side Stretch
exercises.description: Lift your arms and gently arc your torso to each side, keeping both feet grounded. This standing stretch lengthens the sides of your waist and explores movement around your ribs.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and weight even across both feet.
Raise both arms overhead, keeping your elbows soft and neck relaxed.
Lean gently right, reaching upward through your left fingertips.
Return to center, then lean left through your right fingertips.
Alternate slowly, inhaling at center and exhaling into each side bend.
exercises.breath: Inhale at center, exhale to lean
exercises.cue: Grow tall before you arc
exercises.tip: Keep your hands on your hips if lifting your arms feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Seated Shake Out
exercises.description: Sitting tall, you shake out your hands and let the shake run through your arms, shoulders and a lively bounce of the knees. It wakes up the whole body before seated practice.
steps: Sit tall near the front of your chair, feet flat.
Lift your hands and shake them out with loose wrists.
Let the shake travel up through your arms and shoulders.
Add a little bounce of the knees and heels.
Keep it lively, then slow down and rest your hands.
exercises.breath: Breathe freely as you shake
exercises.cue: Shake the sleepiness out of your body
exercises.tip: Keep your back tall and your face soft while everything else shakes.

exercises.name: Guided Deep Breathing
exercises.description: Sit tall and rest your hands over your lower belly, noticing its gentle movement with each breath. This quiet practice builds breath awareness and helps you settle into a comfortable seated posture.
steps: Sit comfortably on your chair with both feet flat.
Rest your hands lightly over your lower belly.
Inhale through your nose, letting your belly gently expand.
Exhale slowly, allowing your belly to soften back inward.
Continue at an easy pace without forcing deeper breaths.
exercises.breath: Inhale gently, exhale slowly and easily
exercises.cue: Let your breath arrive like a tide
exercises.tip: Keep each breath comfortable rather than large, and return to normal breathing if lightheaded.

exercises.name: Commencement (Opening Form)
exercises.description: Float your hands toward your chest, then let them descend as you sit comfortably upright. Matching this simple lift and lower with your breath encourages relaxed shoulders and smoother arm control.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with arms resting beside you.
Inhale and float your hands forward toward chest height.
Soften your elbows and angle your fingertips gently upward.
Exhale and lower your hands slowly toward your thighs.
Repeat gently, letting each breath guide the lift and lowering.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to lower
exercises.cue: Float up, settle like falling leaves
exercises.tip: Lift only as high as comfortable, keeping your shoulders away from your ears.

exercises.name: Seated Waist Circles
exercises.description: Hands on your waist, you circle your upper body in big, smooth rings over your knees. It loosens the spine and waist and warms the core without leaving your chair.
steps: Sit near the front of your chair, feet wide and flat.
Place your hands on your waist and sit tall.
Lean forward and circle your chest out over your right knee.
Circle back and out over your left knee, smooth and wide.
Make two circles each way, then sit upright.
exercises.breath: Breathe slowly through each circle
exercises.cue: Stir a big pot with your chest
exercises.tip: Keep both sitting bones on the seat so the movement stays in the waist.

exercises.name: Lifting the Qi
exercises.description: You scoop your hands up the front of your body to above your head, then press them slowly down again. This slow seated flow links movement and breath and leaves you calm and centred.
steps: Sit tall with feet flat and hands beside your hips.
Turn your palms up and scoop your hands forward.
Inhale as you lift them slowly up to above your head.
Turn your palms down and exhale as you press them down.
Repeat slowly, letting the breath lead the hands.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to press
exercises.cue: Lift the light up, press the calm down
exercises.tip: Keep the shoulders low and the elbows soft so the arms stay round and easy.

exercises.name: Holding the Ball
exercises.description: Shape your arms around an imaginary ball and carry it gently from side to side, switching which hand is higher. This rounded pattern develops coordinated arm movement while encouraging relaxed shoulders.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with both feet resting flat.
Raise your hands before your chest, palms facing around an imaginary ball.
Move the ball right, right hand near chest, left palm beneath.
Return through center, then move left with your left hand higher.
Continue alternating, inhaling at center and exhaling toward each side.
exercises.breath: Inhale at center, exhale to shift
exercises.cue: Cradle a light, round ball
exercises.tip: Keep the imaginary ball close enough that your elbows remain comfortably bent.

exercises.name: Pulling Down the Heavens
exercises.description: Float both arms upward, then lower your hands slowly in front of you as your feet stay grounded. This spacious reach practices overhead shoulder mobility and pairs a controlled lowering with an easy exhale.
steps: Sit tall on your chair, feet flat and hands beside your hips.
Inhale and sweep both arms outward and upward, keeping elbows soft.
Reach overhead only as far as your shoulders comfortably allow.
Turn your palms downward and lower your hands in front of you.
Exhale through the descent, then repeat at an unhurried pace.
exercises.breath: Inhale to rise, exhale to lower
exercises.cue: Draw the sky gently downward
exercises.tip: Stop the lift below overhead if you need to arch your back to reach.

exercises.name: Pushing the Mountain
exercises.description: Press both palms forward from your chest, then draw them back without leaning away from the chair. This gentle push and return builds controlled reaching and coordinates your arms with your breath.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with feet flat and arms relaxed.
Lift your hands to chest height with your palms facing forward.
Exhale and press both palms forward, leaving your elbows slightly bent.
Inhale and draw your hands back toward your chest.
Repeat the gentle push and return without rocking your torso.
exercises.breath: Exhale to push, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Press through soft, still air
exercises.tip: Keep your wrists comfortably aligned, and shorten the reach if your shoulders feel tense.

exercises.name: Wave Hands Like Clouds
exercises.description: Glide one hand across your chest, then let the other take its place in a soft, alternating wave. This flowing pattern practices shoulder mobility and coordination while your seated base stays quiet.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with feet flat and arms resting.
Lift your right hand before your chest, palm facing inward.
Sweep your right hand from left to right, then lower it.
Lift your left hand and sweep from right to left.
Continue alternating gently, keeping your torso quiet and breathing naturally.
exercises.breath: Breathe naturally as your hands glide
exercises.cue: Let your hands drift like clouds
exercises.tip: Keep each sweep below shoulder height, with soft elbows and plenty of space around you.

exercises.name: Washing the Face with Qi
exercises.description: You sweep your palms up in front of your face, over the head and down the back of the neck. This soothing gesture releases tension from the face and neck and settles the mind.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with both feet flat.
Bring your palms up in front of your face, not touching.
Sweep them up over your forehead and the top of your head.
Draw them down the back of your neck and over the shoulders.
Lower your hands to your thighs and let your eyes soften.
exercises.breath: Inhale to rise, exhale to sweep down
exercises.cue: Wash away the day with your hands
exercises.tip: Move slowly and let the eyes close gently as the hands pass the face.

exercises.name: Stroke the Bird’s Tail
exercises.description: Raise one palm forward while the other settles near your belly, following the lifted hand with your gaze. Alternating sides develops coordinated arm movement and gentle neck mobility while you stay grounded.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with feet flat and shoulders relaxed.
Lift your left hand forward to shoulder height, palm facing outward.
Bring your right palm upward near your belly, eyes following your left hand.
Exhale and lower both hands, returning your gaze to center.
Repeat on the opposite side, moving slowly with each breath.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to return
exercises.cue: Follow a bird's gentle flight
exercises.tip: Follow with your eyes only if turning your head feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Catch the Moon
exercises.description: You turn and reach up over one shoulder as if holding the moon, then circle down past your knees to catch it on the other side. It rotates the spine and stretches the sides in one flowing figure.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with feet flat.
Turn to the left and reach both hands up over your shoulder.
Let your gaze follow your hands as if holding the moon.
Circle the hands down past your knees and up to the right.
Flow side to side in one smooth, unbroken figure.
exercises.breath: Inhale to reach, exhale to circle down
exercises.cue: Hold the moon gently in your hands
exercises.tip: Keep the hips facing forward; the turn comes from the waist and chest.

exercises.name: Phoenix Wings
exercises.description: You sweep both arms out and up like wide wings until the hands meet overhead, then float them down again. It opens the chest and shoulders with a graceful, breath-led rhythm.
steps: Sit tall on your chair with feet flat.
Inhale and sweep both arms out to the sides.
Keep lifting until your hands meet above your head.
Exhale and float the wings down in a wide arc.
Cross the wrists at your belly, then rise again.
exercises.breath: Inhale to rise, exhale to float down
exercises.cue: Spread your wings slowly and wide
exercises.tip: Lead with the wrists and let the fingers trail softly behind.

exercises.name: Front & Back Step Touch
exercises.description: Tap one heel forward and the same toes behind you, returning to center between taps. This rhythmic pattern practices directional foot placement and standing balance while keeping your legs moving at an easy pace.
steps: Stand tall with feet close together and knees softly bent.
Reach your right foot forward, lightly tapping your heel on the floor.
Bring your right foot beside your left, then tap your right toes behind.
Return to center and repeat the pattern with your left foot.
Alternate sides at a steady pace, breathing easily throughout.
exercises.breath: Keep your breathing easy and steady
exercises.cue: Tap lightly, then find your center
exercises.tip: Keep each tap close to your body so your standing foot stays firmly grounded.

exercises.name: Hamstring Curl High Knee Combo
exercises.description: Alternate heel curls behind you, then change to knee lifts in front. This combination works the backs and fronts of your thighs while building coordination and a steady walking rhythm.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your shoulders relaxed.
Bend one knee, bringing your heel back, then alternate legs.
Complete four curls, then lift alternating knees in front four times.
Repeat the combination smoothly, swinging your arms with your steps.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly through each change
exercises.cue: Heels back, knees forward
exercises.tip: Keep your knee lifts low enough to stay upright without leaning backward.

exercises.name: Heel Pedals
exercises.description: Hands on hips, you pedal your heels up and down in place with a light bounce, toes staying on the floor. It warms the calves and ankles quickly and keeps your feet springy.
steps: Stand tall with your hands on your hips.
Lift your right heel as the left heel presses down.
Switch quickly, pedalling the heels in place.
Keep a light bounce with the toes on the floor.
Stay tall and keep a fast, steady rhythm.
exercises.breath: Breathe naturally with the rhythm
exercises.cue: Pedal a bike with your heels
exercises.tip: Keep the knees soft and the weight centred, not rocking forward.

exercises.name: High Knee Side Tap
exercises.description: You drive one knee up while pulling your elbows down, then tap that foot out to the side as the arms reach up. It is a bouncy, full-body cardio move that gets your heart going fast.
steps: Stand tall with your hands raised to shoulder height.
Drive your left knee up as you pull your elbows down.
Tap that foot out to the side as your arms reach up.
Repeat on the right side.
Keep switching sides with light, springy steps.
exercises.breath: Exhale as the knee lifts
exercises.cue: Knee up, tap out, reach high
exercises.tip: Land softly through the ball of the foot and keep the chest lifted.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.description: March in place, lifting each knee toward your waist without leaning back. The higher steps engage your hip muscles and build walking stamina while you practice balancing briefly on each leg.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed.
Gently firm your belly and lift one knee forward.
Lower your foot softly, then lift the opposite knee.
Continue alternating knee lifts, swinging your arms at a steady pace.
exercises.breath: Keep breathing evenly with your steps
exercises.cue: Stay tall as knees rise
exercises.tip: Lift only as high as you can while keeping your torso upright.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Calf Stretch
exercises.description: Step one foot back and ease your weight forward with the back heel grounded. This standing stretch lengthens your calf and the front of your hip to support a more comfortable stride.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips.
Step your right foot back, keeping both feet pointing forward.
Bend your front knee gently and press your back heel down.
Keep your chest upright and lightly tuck your pelvis under.
Hold for several easy breaths, then switch your legs.
exercises.breath: Exhale gently as you settle
exercises.cue: Root your heel, rise tall
exercises.tip: Shorten your stance if your back heel lifts or your lower back arches.

exercises.name: Inner Thigh Side Stretch
exercises.description: Shift into one bent knee while sending your hips back and lengthening the opposite leg. This side stretch opens your inner thighs and helps you explore a comfortable sideways weight shift.
steps: Stand with feet wider than your hips, toes facing forward.
Rest your hands on your thighs and send your hips backward.
Bend your right knee while keeping your left leg comfortably long.
Slide your hands toward your right thigh, keeping your chest open.
Pause for easy breaths, then return through center and switch sides.
exercises.breath: Exhale into the gentle side shift
exercises.cue: Sit back into one hip
exercises.tip: Keep your hands above your knees and make the bend shallow if needed.

exercises.name: March in Place
exercises.description: Take alternating steps in place while swinging your arms naturally beside you. This familiar movement warms your legs and builds a steady rhythm for comfortable, low-impact activity.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and knees relaxed.
Lift one foot slightly, then place it softly beneath your hip.
Alternate your steps while swinging the opposite arm forward.
Keep marching at a pace that lets you speak comfortably.
exercises.breath: Breathe steadily with your marching rhythm
exercises.cue: Quiet feet, easy arms
exercises.tip: Start with small steps, increasing your pace only while your landings stay quiet.

exercises.name: March with Heel Tap
exercises.description: March in place for three steps, then lift one heel behind you and tap it with the opposite hand. The behind-the-body reach adds coordination and a gentle quad stretch to a lively march.
steps: March in place for three easy steps, chest tall.
Lift your right heel behind you and tap it with your left hand.
March three more steps, then lift your left heel behind you.
Tap it with your right hand and keep the pattern flowing.
exercises.breath: Breathe in rhythm with your steps
exercises.cue: March, march, march, tap
exercises.tip: Keep the foot low and reach toward your ankle without needing to touch it.

exercises.name: Shoulder Hug Stretch
exercises.description: Wrap your arms around your upper body, then switch which arm rests on top. This gentle hug stretches the backs of your shoulders and encourages your upper back to soften.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees comfortably soft.
Wrap your arms across your chest, reaching toward opposite shoulder blades.
Let your shoulders settle as your elbows ease forward.
Release slowly, then repeat with the other arm on top.
Breathe slowly, allowing each hug to feel gentle and unforced.
exercises.breath: Exhale gently into your hug
exercises.cue: Wrap yourself in a soft blanket
exercises.tip: Rest your hands on your upper arms if reaching farther feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Side Bend Stretch
exercises.description: Reach one arm overhead and gently bend toward the opposite side, keeping both feet grounded. This stretch lengthens the side of your torso and helps you practice controlled sideways movement.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Rest your left hand on your hip and raise your right arm.
Bend gently left, keeping your chest forward and both feet grounded.
Return upright, lower your arm, and switch sides.
Alternate slowly, exhaling into each small side bend.
exercises.breath: Inhale upright, exhale into the bend
exercises.cue: Make a gentle crescent shape
exercises.tip: Keep your raised hand lower if reaching overhead feels uncomfortable for your shoulder.

exercises.name: Side Tap Overhead Hook
exercises.description: You tap one foot out to the side while hooking the opposite arm over your head in a big arc. It stretches the sides of the body and keeps your heart rate climbing.
steps: Stand tall with feet together.
Tap your left foot out to the side.
At the same time, hook your right arm up and over your head.
Return, then tap right and hook the left arm over.
Keep switching sides with a lively, steady rhythm.
exercises.breath: Breathe out with each hook
exercises.cue: Tap out and reach over
exercises.tip: Reach long through the fingertips and keep the hips facing forward.

exercises.name: Standing Core Twist
exercises.description: Lift your bent arms to chest height and turn your rib cage from side to side while your hips stay facing forward. The controlled rotation loosens the spine and wakes up the waist after walking.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Lift your bent arms to chest height, elbows wide.
Turn your rib cage to the right, hips facing forward.
Turn back through center to the left and keep flowing.
exercises.breath: Exhale as you turn, inhale through center
exercises.cue: Turn from the waist, hips stay still
exercises.tip: Keep the twist small enough that your knees stay aligned with your toes.

exercises.name: Cross-Back Step with Arm Swing
exercises.description: You step one foot back behind the other in a curtsy step while swinging both arms across your body. It works the glutes and legs and keeps your feet light and quick.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Step your left foot back behind your right leg.
Swing both arms across your body to the right.
Return, then step the right foot back and swing left.
Keep alternating at a brisk, light pace.
exercises.breath: Breathe out on each step back
exercises.cue: Curtsy and swing
exercises.tip: Keep the front knee over the toes and the steps light.

exercises.name: Cross Behind Step Arms Up
exercises.description: Step one foot slightly behind the other as you lift both arms, then return and switch sides. Combining crossed footwork with an upward reach challenges coordination and control during weight shifts.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and arms lowered.
Step your right foot slightly behind and across your left.
Lift both arms forward and upward within a comfortable range.
Return your right foot home as you lower both arms.
Alternate sides slowly, exhaling as you lift your arms.
exercises.breath: Exhale to reach, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Reach tall, keep your steps small
exercises.tip: Keep your arms below shoulder height and reduce the crossing distance if you feel unsteady.

exercises.name: Front Toe Tap Pull Down
exercises.description: Tap one toe forward as you draw both elbows down toward your ribs, then switch feet. Pairing your arm pull with each tap develops coordination and adds gentle upper-body effort.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your shoulders relaxed.
Raise both hands overhead only as far as feels comfortable.
Tap your right toes forward while drawing both elbows toward your ribs.
Return your foot beneath you as your hands rise again.
Alternate forward toe taps and arm pulls at a steady pace.
exercises.breath: Exhale to pull, inhale to reach
exercises.cue: Pull down two soft ribbons
exercises.tip: Reach only to shoulder height if lifting your arms higher feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Hamstring Curl Arms In
exercises.description: Step from side to side, bending each knee to lift your heel behind you as your arms draw inward. This combination works the backs of your thighs while building arm and leg coordination.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms reaching forward.
Step right and bend your left knee, lifting your heel behind you.
Draw both elbows back beside your ribs as your heel lifts.
Lower your foot and reach forward before switching sides.
Alternate heel curls and arm pulls with an easy, steady rhythm.
exercises.breath: Exhale to curl, inhale to reset
exercises.cue: Draw your elbows into home base
exercises.tip: Keep your knees pointing downward rather than arching your back to lift your heels higher.

exercises.name: Arms-Up Knee Lifts
exercises.description: Reach both arms overhead and drive one knee up at a time in a steady rhythm. Holding the arms high while the knees lift raises your heart rate and works your shoulders and core together.
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width, and reach both arms overhead.
Lift your right knee toward hip height, then lower it softly.
Lift your left knee, keeping your chest tall and arms up.
Keep alternating in a brisk, even rhythm.
exercises.breath: Breathe steadily with the rhythm
exercises.cue: Tall arms, quick light knees
exercises.tip: Keep your hands at shoulder height and use knee lifts for an easier option.

exercises.name: Knee Lift Clap
exercises.description: Lift one knee toward your waist and bring your hands together underneath your thigh, then change sides. The clap gives your march a clear rhythm while challenging coordination and single-leg balance.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed.
Shift onto your left foot and lift your right knee comfortably.
Bring your hands beneath your raised thigh for a gentle clap.
Lower your foot, stand tall, and repeat with your left knee.
Alternate knee lifts and claps with an easy marching rhythm.
exercises.breath: Exhale to lift, inhale to lower
exercises.cue: Bring your knee toward the clap
exercises.tip: If reaching underneath makes you bend forward, clap above your thigh instead.

exercises.name: Knee Lift Opposite Elbow
exercises.description: Raise one knee and gently turn your upper body to bring the opposite elbow toward it. Alternating this diagonal movement develops cross-body coordination and trunk control while keeping your march active.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your elbows comfortably bent.
Lift your right knee while turning your chest slightly toward it.
Bring your left elbow toward your right knee without rounding your back.
Lower your foot and return your chest to face forward.
Alternate sides at an easy pace, exhaling with each knee lift.
exercises.breath: Exhale to lift, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Connect across your body's diagonal
exercises.tip: Leave space between your elbow and knee rather than forcing them to touch.

exercises.name: Rolling Arms Side Step
exercises.description: Step side to side while circling your forearms around each other in front of your chest. Combining smooth arm rolls with lateral steps builds coordination and keeps your shoulders gently moving.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your elbows bent.
Hold your forearms in front of your chest with relaxed hands.
Step right and bring your left foot alongside without crossing.
Circle your forearms around each other as you step left.
Continue stepping side to side with smooth rolls and steady breathing.
exercises.breath: Breathe steadily through rolls and steps
exercises.cue: Roll your arms like gentle wheels
exercises.tip: Make smaller circles and lower your elbows if your shoulders begin to tire.

exercises.name: Side Step Punch
exercises.description: Step from side to side as you send alternating punches forward at chest height. This pairing builds arm and leg coordination while keeping your whole body moving at a steady pace.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and hands near your chest.
Step right and punch your left hand forward without locking your elbow.
Bring your left foot inward and draw your hand back.
Step left and punch your right hand forward, then return.
Alternate sides at an even pace, breathing freely as you move.
exercises.breath: Exhale to punch, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Send each punch through soft air
exercises.tip: Keep your punches below shoulder height and shorten your steps if you feel unsteady.

exercises.name: Side Step Pull Back
exercises.description: Travel gently from side to side while drawing one elbow back beside your waist. The alternating pull engages your upper back and helps you coordinate arm movement with lateral steps.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms reaching loosely forward.
Step right as you draw your right elbow toward your waist.
Tap your left foot inward and reach your right arm forward.
Step left, draw your left elbow back, then tap inward.
Continue alternating sides, keeping your pulls smooth and your breathing easy.
exercises.breath: Exhale to pull, inhale to reach
exercises.cue: Slide your elbow into a pocket
exercises.tip: Keep your chest facing forward rather than twisting your body with each pull.

exercises.name: Side Step Pull Down
exercises.description: Step sideways while drawing both elbows down from a comfortable overhead reach. This flowing combination engages your back and shoulders while adding upper-body work to your steady stepping rhythm.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and arms relaxed.
Raise both arms overhead only as far as feels comfortable.
Step right and draw both elbows down toward your ribs.
Tap your left foot inward as you reach upward again.
Repeat toward the left, then alternate sides with smooth, easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Inhale to reach, exhale to pull
exercises.cue: Draw the sky toward your ribs
exercises.tip: Reach only to shoulder height if lifting overhead makes your shoulders uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Side Step Squeeze Back
exercises.description: You step wide side to side while pulling both elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades. It raises your heart rate and strengthens the upper back for better posture.
steps: Stand tall with arms reaching forward at chest height.
Step wide to your left and bring your feet together.
Pull both elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Reach forward again and step wide to your right.
Keep moving side to side in a brisk rhythm.
exercises.breath: Exhale as you squeeze
exercises.cue: Step wide and squeeze the back
exercises.tip: Keep the shoulders down as you squeeze, chest proud and open.

exercises.name: Side Steps Cross Arms
exercises.description: Step from side to side while opening your arms and crossing them loosely in front. The sweeping pattern works your shoulders and helps you coordinate your upper body with sideways travel.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed beside your body.
Step right and open both arms below shoulder height, palms down.
Tap your left foot inward and loosely cross your forearms in front.
Step left, open your arms, then tap inward and cross again.
Continue smoothly, alternating which arm crosses on top each time.
exercises.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to cross
exercises.cue: Sweep your arms like soft curtains
exercises.tip: Keep your arm sweeps small enough that your shoulders stay relaxed throughout.

exercises.name: Side Tap Arms Up
exercises.description: Tap one foot out to the side as both arms reach upward, then return and switch. This light, alternating pattern practices weight control and shoulder movement without adding a hop.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, arms down, and knees gently softened.
Shift your weight left and tap your right toes sideways.
Raise both arms comfortably upward as your toes touch down.
Return your right foot and lower your arms, then switch sides.
Alternate light taps and smooth reaches while keeping your breathing steady.
exercises.breath: Inhale to reach, exhale to lower
exercises.cue: Tap lightly, reach toward the sky
exercises.tip: Keep your tapping foot close and reach lower if your balance feels uncertain.

exercises.name: Broadening Chest
exercises.description: Float both arms forward, open them wide, then gather them back toward the center. This gentle sequence explores chest and shoulder mobility while matching your movement to a slow, comfortable breath.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and arms resting down.
Raise both arms forward to chest height, keeping your elbows soft.
Inhale slowly and open your arms sideways, letting your chest broaden.
Exhale as you bring your arms forward and gently lower them.
Repeat the flowing sequence, letting your breath guide your pace.
exercises.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to gather
exercises.cue: Open your arms like unfolding wings
exercises.tip: Open only as wide as feels easy, keeping your ribs relaxed over your hips.

exercises.name: Cat Walk
exercises.description: Take small backward steps as your arms open and gather toward your waist. This slow walking pattern builds awareness of weight changes and control through your feet.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and spine tall.
Shift your weight onto one leg and open your arms gently.
Step the other foot slightly backward, touching your toes down first.
Lower that heel gently as your hands return toward your waist.
Alternate feet slowly, breathing evenly as you transfer your weight.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly through each small step
exercises.cue: Step as quietly as a cat
exercises.tip: Keep your steps small, and check that the space behind you is clear.

exercises.name: Circling Arms Separate the Clouds
exercises.description: Lift your hands in front of you, then circle them outward and down in broad, gentle arcs. The continuous motion encourages shoulder mobility and connects your arm movements with your breath.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms resting at your sides.
Lift both hands in front of you with softly bent elbows.
Circle your arms outward, then lower them gently toward your sides.
Repeat smoothly, inhaling to lift and exhaling to circle down.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to circle
exercises.cue: Part the clouds with soft hands
exercises.tip: Make your circles smaller if your shoulders rise toward your ears.

exercises.name: Embracing the Center
exercises.description: Open your arms with palms facing up, then gather your hands toward your chest as your knees soften. This gentle gathering motion coordinates your upper and lower body while practicing balanced, centered standing.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees comfortably soft.
Inhale and spread your arms sideways with palms facing upward.
Exhale and draw your hands inward toward your chest.
Bend your knees slightly, keeping your weight even across both feet.
Repeat the opening and gathering with a slow, comfortable breath.
exercises.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to gather
exercises.cue: Gather a little space toward you
exercises.tip: Bend your knees only slightly, keeping them pointing in the same direction as your toes.

exercises.name: Holding a Ball in Front of the Shoulder
exercises.description: Round your arms around an imaginary ball and carry it gently from side to side. The movement links relaxed shoulder control with small weight shifts, helping you move as one coordinated whole.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and shoulders relaxed.
Round both arms before your chest as though holding a ball.
Carry your hands toward one shoulder, shifting weight toward that foot.
Guide your hands across toward the other shoulder, shifting weight gently.
Continue side to side with easy breathing and soft elbows.
exercises.breath: Breathe easily as the ball travels
exercises.cue: Carry a ball made of air
exercises.tip: Keep both feet planted, and let your hands travel only as far as feels easy.

exercises.name: Lifting the Sky
exercises.description: You lift interlaced hands up the centre of your body to a full overhead stretch and rise onto the balls of your feet. It lengthens the whole body, opens the chest and builds balance.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed.
Interlace your fingers in front of your belly.
Inhale and lift your hands up and overhead, palms to the sky.
Rise onto the balls of your feet and stretch tall.
Exhale, lower your heels and open your arms down to your sides.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to lower
exercises.cue: Push the sky away with your palms
exercises.tip: Rise only as high as you can stay steady; the stretch matters more than the height.

exercises.name: Painting a Rainbow
exercises.description: Curve one arm above your head as your weight drifts gently toward the opposite foot, then change sides. This flowing reach explores side-body length and builds control during small sideways weight shifts.
steps: Stand with feet comfortably wide, knees soft, and arms relaxed.
Lift your right arm into a gentle curve above your head.
Shift slightly toward your left foot, keeping both feet planted.
Lower your right arm and switch arms as you shift right.
Continue alternating sides slowly, breathing naturally through each curved reach.
exercises.breath: Breathe naturally through each sweeping reach
exercises.cue: Trace a rainbow across the sky
exercises.tip: Keep the reach low enough to relax your shoulder, and avoid leaning far sideways.

exercises.name: Punching in Horse Stance
exercises.description: From a wide horse stance with fists at your waist, punch slowly forward one arm at a time. The steady stance builds leg strength while each punch focuses the mind.
steps: Sink into a wide horse stance, loose fists at your waist.
Punch your left fist slowly forward, turning it palm down.
Draw it back to your waist as the right fist punches.
Keep alternating with strong, unhurried punches.
exercises.breath: Exhale with each punch
exercises.cue: Power from the legs, calm face
exercises.tip: Keep your fingers loosely curled and stop each punch before your elbow straightens fully.

exercises.name: Cloud Hands in Horse Stance
exercises.description: Sink into a wide horse stance and let your hands wave past your face like drifting clouds as your waist turns side to side. The low stance strengthens the legs while the arms stay soft and flowing.
steps: Step wide and bend your knees over your toes.
Float your right palm past your face as your waist turns right.
Let the left hand circle low in front of your belly.
Change hands and turn left, waving like clouds.
exercises.breath: Inhale as you turn, exhale as hands pass
exercises.cue: Legs rooted, hands like clouds
exercises.tip: Use a shallower knee bend if your legs tire or your knees feel uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Rowing Boat in the Middle of Lake
exercises.description: Tip forward gently as your arms reach out, then draw them back as you stand tall. This rowing pattern coordinates your shoulders and hips while encouraging smooth changes in posture.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees gently bent.
Hinge slightly at your hips and reach both arms forward.
Draw your elbows back beside your ribs as you stand tall.
Reach forward again, keeping your neck aligned with your spine.
Repeat smoothly, inhaling to reach and exhaling to draw back.
exercises.breath: Inhale forward, exhale as you draw back
exercises.cue: Pull your oars through quiet water
exercises.tip: Keep the forward hinge small and avoid rounding your back to reach farther.

exercises.name: Twisting Arm Swings
exercises.description: You turn from the waist side to side and let your loose arms swing around you, tapping shoulder and lower back. It unwinds the spine and releases the shoulders with an easy, hypnotic rhythm.
steps: Stand with feet a little wider than your hips, knees soft.
Turn your waist to the right and let your arms swing.
Turn to the left and let the arms wrap around you.
Let one hand tap the shoulder and the other the lower back.
Keep the feet planted and swing in a steady, relaxed rhythm.
exercises.breath: Breathe out on each turn
exercises.cue: Arms like empty sleeves in the wind
exercises.tip: Let the arms stay completely loose; the waist does all the work.

exercises.name: Turning to Look at the Moon
exercises.description: Turn your chest and head gently to one side, lifting a hand as though framing the moon. This slow exploration of rotation helps you coordinate your gaze and upper body while staying balanced.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and arms relaxed.
Turn your chest and head gently toward the right.
Lift your right hand slightly, letting your eyes follow comfortably.
Lower your hand and return your chest to center.
Repeat toward the left, alternating sides with unhurried breaths.
exercises.breath: Inhale to turn, exhale to return
exercises.cue: Find the moon beside you
exercises.tip: Keep your gaze near eye level if looking upward feels uncomfortable or unsteady.

exercises.name: Twisting Waist and Pushing Palms
exercises.description: Turn your torso gently as one palm presses forward and the other rests near your waist. This coordinated push develops controlled shoulder movement and helps you maintain balance while rotating.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and hands near waist.
Turn your torso gently left as your right palm presses forward.
Keep your left hand near your waist and both knees relaxed.
Return to center, then turn right and press your left palm.
Alternate slowly, exhaling with each press and inhaling back to center.
exercises.breath: Exhale to press, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Press gently through warm water
exercises.tip: Keep a slight bend in your pressing elbow and avoid twisting through your knees.

exercises.name: Pushing Waves
exercises.description: In a bow stance, rock back as your palms draw in, then rock forward as they push out like a wave. The rhythmic weight shift strengthens the legs and steadies the breath.
steps: Step your left foot forward into a gentle bow stance.
Shift back onto the rear leg, front toes lifting, palms drawing in.
Shift forward onto the front leg as both palms push out.
Rock back and forth smoothly, like waves on a shore.
exercises.breath: Inhale back, exhale forward
exercises.cue: Ride the wave, back and forth
exercises.tip: Keep both feet grounded and make your weight shift smaller if you feel unsteady.

exercises.name: Commencing Form and Regulating Breathing
exercises.description: Float your hands to shoulder height, then lower them as your knees soften. Matching this gentle rise and fall to your breath helps you coordinate your arms and legs without rushing.
steps: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, arms resting beside you.
Inhale and float your wrists forward to shoulder height, palms down.
Exhale, soften your knees, and lower your palms toward your hips.
Repeat smoothly, gently straightening your legs as your hands rise.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to lower
exercises.cue: Float up, settle like a feather
exercises.tip: Keep your knee bend shallow and let your breath stay comfortable rather than forced.

exercises.name: Concentrating with Your Mind For Energy
exercises.description: Rest your hands over your lower belly and stand quietly, noticing the gentle movement beneath your palms. This still practice helps you recognize your breathing rhythm and unnecessary tension in your stance.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Rest your hands over your lower belly and relax your shoulders.
Keep your gaze soft, noticing your belly move beneath your hands.
Breathe easily, imagining warmth gathering inward and settling with each exhale.
exercises.breath: Breathe naturally, without forcing depth
exercises.cue: Let warmth settle beneath your hands
exercises.tip: Keep your eyes open and your gaze steady if closing them affects your balance.

exercises.name: Guided Deep Breathing
exercises.description: Stand comfortably with one hand on your chest and the other on your belly, noticing each slow breath. This practice builds awareness of your breathing while encouraging an easy, upright stance.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your knees soft.
Place one hand on your chest, the other on your belly.
Inhale through your nose, letting your belly gently expand.
Exhale comfortably, allowing your belly to settle without pressing inward.
Continue at an easy pace, keeping each breath unforced.
exercises.breath: Inhale gently, exhale without pushing
exercises.cue: Let your breath widen your waist
exercises.tip: Keep your breaths comfortable rather than extra deep, especially if you feel lightheaded.

exercises.name: Repulse the Monkey
exercises.description: Step slowly backward while your arms trade places, one palm pushing forward as the other circles back past your ear. Walking backward with control is rare in daily life and builds real confidence on your feet.
steps: Push your right palm forward, left hand resting palm up by your waist.
Lift your left foot and place it one step behind you, toes first.
Sit back onto that foot as your left hand circles back and up past your ear.
Push the left palm forward while the right hand draws back to your waist.
Step back with the other foot and let the arms trade again.
exercises.breath: Exhale with each forward push
exercises.cue: Step back, push forward
exercises.tip: Place each foot down toes first, a little to the side, so your stance never narrows to a tightrope.

exercises.name: Commencement (Opening Form)
exercises.description: Float both arms to chest height, open your hands outward, then gather them back and lower. Pairing this gentle arm pattern with your breath encourages shoulder mobility and controlled movement while standing.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms resting by your sides.
Inhale and float both arms forward to chest height, elbows soft.
Lift your fingertips gently and open your hands slightly outward.
Bring your hands toward center, then exhale as your arms lower.
Repeat smoothly, letting your breath set a comfortable pace.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to lower
exercises.cue: Float your hands on rising water
exercises.tip: Raise your arms only as high as you can without lifting your shoulders.

exercises.name: Holding the Ball
exercises.description: Shape your arms around an imaginary ball and carry it side to side as your weight shifts. You practice coordinated hand changes and controlled balance without lifting your feet.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees relaxed, and arms loose.
Raise your hands before your chest, palms facing each other.
Shift right, placing your right hand above and left hand below.
Shift left, switching hands so your left hand rests above.
Alternate smoothly with relaxed breaths, keeping both feet on the floor.
exercises.breath: Keep your breath soft and steady
exercises.cue: Carry a ball light as air
exercises.tip: Keep your weight shifts small enough that both feet stay comfortably grounded.

exercises.name: Pulling Down the Heavens
exercises.description: Sweep your arms wide and overhead, then lower your hands slowly in front as your knees soften. You coordinate a broad shoulder movement with a steady breath and gentle leg control.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees relaxed, and arms hanging loosely.
Inhale and sweep your arms outward and overhead, palms facing each other.
Exhale and lower your hands down your front, palms facing inward.
Soften your knees slightly as your hands pass your chest.
Repeat smoothly, letting your breath guide the rise and fall.
exercises.breath: Inhale to rise, exhale to lower
exercises.cue: Draw the sky gently toward you
exercises.tip: Raise your arms only as high as you can without arching your lower back.

exercises.name: Pushing the Mountain
exercises.description: From a short staggered stance, press your palms forward and draw them back toward your chest. You build control through your arms while practicing steady posture and a relaxed, deliberate exhale.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, then step one foot slightly forward.
Inhale and bring your hands to chest height, palms facing forward.
Exhale and press both palms forward, leaving your elbows slightly bent.
Inhale and draw your hands back toward your chest.
Repeat slowly, keeping your weight comfortably balanced between both feet.
exercises.breath: Exhale to press, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Press slowly through soft clay
exercises.tip: Use a short stance and avoid leaning your chest forward as you press.

exercises.name: Wave Hands Like Clouds
exercises.description: Float one hand across your chest as your torso turns, then trade hands and return the other way. You develop flowing arm coordination while practicing gentle rotation and side-to-side balance.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and arms relaxed.
Raise your right hand before your chest, palm facing inward.
Float your right hand rightward, turning your torso and shifting weight gently.
Lower your right hand, raise your left, and turn left.
Continue alternating smoothly with easy breaths, then rest your arms.
exercises.breath: Breathe softly through each passing cloud
exercises.cue: Let your hands drift like clouds
exercises.tip: Keep your hands below eye level and let your torso guide their travel.

exercises.name: Stroke the Bird’s Tail
exercises.description: Reach one hand forward and the other back, then take a small step as your arms sweep down. You practice controlled weight shifts while coordinating your hands, feet, and gentle torso turns.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, then shift weight onto your right leg.
Turn slightly left, reaching left palm down forward and right palm up behind.
Step your left foot forward and sweep both arms diagonally downward.
Turn your chest slightly right, keeping both knees soft.
Return to your starting stance and alternate sides with easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Inhale to reach, exhale to sweep
exercises.cue: Sweep a feather through the air
exercises.tip: Keep each step short and let your knees follow your toes as you turn.

exercises.name: White Crane Spreads Wings
exercises.description: Sit back into your right leg as one hand floats up beside your temple and the other settles by your hip, the front toes barely touching the floor. The third form of the 24 teaches you to stand tall on one leg while your arms open in opposite directions.
steps: From the ball-holding shape, shift your weight back onto your right leg.
Draw your left foot in so only its toes rest lightly on the floor in front.
Float your right hand up beside your right temple, palm turning in.
Press your left hand gently down beside your left hip.
Stay tall and soft for a breath, then lower and flow again.
exercises.breath: Inhale as the wings open · exhale as you settle
exercises.cue: One wing up, one wing down
exercises.tip: Keep nearly all your weight on the back leg; the front toes are only there for balance.

exercises.name: Hand Strums the Lute
exercises.description: Settle onto your back leg, touch the front heel down and bring your hands together in front of you as if cradling a lute. This quiet, compact form trains the empty-stance balance that the stepping forms rely on.
steps: Shift your weight onto your right leg and lift your left foot.
Place your left heel down in front, toes lifted, knee soft.
Raise your left hand to nose height, elbow gently bent.
Bring your right hand in beside your left elbow, palms facing each other.
Sink a little deeper into your back leg and hold the shape calmly.
exercises.breath: Inhale as the hands rise · exhale as you sink
exercises.cue: Sit back and cradle the lute
exercises.tip: If balance wobbles, shorten the distance between your feet rather than leaning back.

exercises.name: Brush Knee and Twist Step
exercises.description: Take a short forward step while one hand brushes past your knee and the other presses ahead. You practice coordinated stepping, gentle trunk rotation, and controlled weight transfer through your legs.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, shifting weight onto your left leg.
Inhale, lifting your left hand near your chest, right hand beside your hip.
Step your right foot forward and brush your right hand past that knee.
Exhale, shift forward, and press your left palm ahead with a gentle turn.
Shift back, return to standing, and repeat on the opposite side.
exercises.breath: Inhale to prepare, exhale to press
exercises.cue: Brush low, press forward, stay tall
exercises.tip: Keep your front knee aligned with your toes and your pressing elbow slightly bent.

exercises.name: Parting the Wild Horse's Mane
exercises.description: Step into a short staggered stance as one hand floats forward and the other settles beside your hip. This coordinated opening helps you practice smooth weight transfers and balanced, upright movement.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees softly bent.
Step your right foot back a little, keeping your stance comfortably wide.
Shift toward your left foot as your left palm floats forward.
Lower your right hand beside your hip, keeping both elbows soft.
Return to center and switch sides, breathing smoothly through each opening.
exercises.breath: Inhale to gather, exhale to open
exercises.cue: Part a curtain with soft hands
exercises.tip: Keep your front knee aligned with your toes, and take a shorter step if needed.

exercises.name: Single Whip
exercises.description: Gather your right fingertips gently, then step left as your left palm opens outward. This broad, flowing shape builds coordination between your hips and arms while you practice shifting weight sideways.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed.
Shift onto your right leg and gently gather your right fingertips together.
Lift your right hand toward shoulder height, keeping your elbow soft.
Step left, shift left, and open your left palm as you turn.
Return to center and repeat on the other side with easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Inhale to gather, exhale to open
exercises.cue: Open your arms like wide wings
exercises.tip: Keep both hands below shoulder height if lifting them higher feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Grasp the Bird’s Tail
exercises.description: Let your hands sweep across your body, gather inward, and press forward as your weight shifts gently. This flowing sequence develops coordinated arm movement and controlled transitions between your feet.
