steps: Stand with your feet comfortably wide, knees soft, hands in front.
Shift right and guide both hands toward your right side.
Shift left as your hands sweep across, letting your waist turn gently.
Draw your hands toward your chest, then press both palms forward softly.
Reverse the sequence slowly, exhaling through each gentle forward press.
exercises.breath: Inhale to gather, exhale to press
exercises.cue: Guide a gentle wave ashore
exercises.tip: Keep your forward press small enough that your shoulders stay above your hips.

exercises.name: High Pat on Horse
exercises.description: Sit into your right leg with the left toes resting forward, then push your right palm out at face height while the left hand draws back to your waist. The form links the Cloud Hands section to the kicks and builds a calm, upright stance.
steps: Shift your weight back onto your right leg.
Draw your left foot in so only the ball of the foot touches the floor.
Circle your right hand up past your ear and push it forward at face height.
Turn your left palm up and draw it back beside your waist.
Stay tall, shoulders soft, and settle into the back leg.
exercises.breath: Exhale as the palm pushes forward
exercises.cue: Reach out, sit back
exercises.tip: Push at chest height instead if raising the hand to face height makes your shoulder lift.

exercises.name: Fair Lady Works the Shuttles
exercises.description: Step into a forward stance as one forearm rolls up to shield your brow and the other palm pushes ahead. Practised to the four corners, it trains diagonal stepping and full-body coordination.
steps: Hold the ball in front of you, right hand on top.
Step your left foot forward and slightly out to the corner.
Shift forward into a bow stance, front knee over the ankle.
Roll your left forearm up in front of your brow, palm turning out.
Push your right palm forward at chest height, then repeat to the other corner.
exercises.breath: Inhale to gather · exhale to push
exercises.cue: Shield high, push through
exercises.tip: Keep the raised arm in front of your brow, not above your head, so your shoulder stays relaxed.

exercises.name: Snake Creeps Down
exercises.description: With one hand hooked behind you, sink into the bent back leg while the front leg straightens and the front hand glides down along it. The lowest form of the 24 builds strong, supple legs; you choose how deep to go.
steps: Form a soft hook with your right hand behind you at shoulder height.
Step your left foot out wide, toes slightly turned in.
Bend your right knee and sit back, letting the left leg lengthen.
Slide your left hand down along the inside of your left leg.
Pause at a depth that feels strong, then rise smoothly.
exercises.breath: Exhale as you sink · inhale as you rise
exercises.cue: Sink like a snake, rise like a tide
exercises.tip: Only sink as far as you can rise back up without pushing on your thigh; a shallow version is still the full form.

exercises.name: Shift the Weight
exercises.description: Move your weight slowly from one foot to the other, keeping both soles on the floor. This quiet practice builds awareness of foot pressure and control before you take a step.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft and arms relaxed.
Shift your weight slowly left, keeping your torso upright.
Feel your left sole press down as your right foot becomes lighter.
Return through center, then shift your weight slowly onto your right foot.
Continue side to side with easy breaths, keeping both feet grounded.
exercises.breath: Breathe slowly without holding your breath
exercises.cue: Pour your weight from foot to foot
exercises.tip: Make each shift smaller if you notice your torso leaning or your knees wobbling.

exercises.name: Sit Step Left Leg
exercises.description: Settle into your right leg, then place your left heel forward and slowly let the foot receive your weight. This deliberate transfer builds confidence in stepping and control through your legs.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and arms relaxed.
Settle your weight over your right foot without leaning sideways.
Reach your left heel forward a short distance, toes pointing ahead.
Lower your left toes and gradually shift weight onto that foot.
Breathe slowly as you settle, keeping your spine comfortably tall.
exercises.breath: Exhale gently as your weight settles
exercises.cue: Pour your weight like warm tea
exercises.tip: Keep your step short enough that you can transfer weight without reaching your torso forward.

exercises.name: Sit Step Right Leg
exercises.description: Sink gently into your left leg, then reach your right heel forward and ease your weight onto the whole foot. This slow transition develops steadier foot placement and balanced control between your legs.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and a soft bend in both knees.
Shift your weight over your left foot, keeping your shoulders level.
Place your right heel slightly forward with your toes pointing ahead.
Ease your right sole down and transfer weight onto your right leg.
Breathe evenly as you settle, leaving your back knee relaxed.
exercises.breath: Breathe out as you settle forward
exercises.cue: Let your front foot receive you
exercises.tip: Let your right knee follow the direction of your toes rather than drifting inward.

exercises.name: Tai Chi Forward Walk
exercises.description: Walk forward with small, quiet steps, placing each heel before gradually settling onto the whole foot. You practice smooth weight transfers and attentive foot placement for more controlled walking.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees gently softened.
Shift onto your right foot and place your left heel forward.
Lower your left sole, then ease your weight onto that leg.
Bring your right foot forward, landing heel first with space between feet.
Continue alternating short steps, breathing naturally and moving without rushing.
exercises.breath: Keep your breathing easy and unhurried
exercises.cue: Walk as though crossing still water
exercises.tip: Keep your feet on separate tracks rather than placing one directly ahead of the other.

exercises.name: Tai Chi Backward Walk
exercises.description: Take small steps backward, touching your toes down before easing each heel toward the floor. You build awareness of foot placement behind you while practicing upright posture and controlled weight shifts.
steps: Stand tall with knees soft and a clear path behind you.
Settle onto your left leg and reach your right foot slightly backward.
Touch your right toes down, then slowly lower your heel.
Shift onto your right foot, keeping your chest lifted and gaze forward.
Alternate small backward steps at an easy, steady breathing rhythm.
exercises.breath: Breathe steadily through each careful step
exercises.cue: Feel the floor before you settle
exercises.tip: Check your path first, and practice beside a stable support if you feel uncertain.

exercises.name: Tai Chi Stance
exercises.description: Stand with your feet comfortably wide, soften your knees, and let your arms rest beside a tall spine. This quiet stance develops awareness of even footing and relaxed, upright alignment.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointing comfortably forward.
Soften both knees and spread your weight evenly across your feet.
Lengthen through your crown and draw your chin back slightly.
Release your shoulders and let your arms hang beside your hips.
Stay comfortably still and breathe slowly without holding your breath.
exercises.breath: Inhale gently, exhale and soften
exercises.cue: Root below and grow tall above
exercises.tip: Use only a small knee bend, keeping your hips comfortably above your knees.

exercises.name: Jogging in Place
exercises.description: Face the wall with both palms resting on it and jog lightly in place, lifting your knees toward hip height. The wall takes care of balance so you can focus on a springy, quiet rhythm that warms your whole body.
steps: Face the wall, feet hip-width apart, palms on the wall at shoulder height.
Lean in very slightly and lengthen your spine from tailbone to crown.
Begin a light jog, lifting one knee and then the other.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, heels kissing the floor.
Find an even, comfortable pace and breathe easily throughout.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly without holding your breath
exercises.cue: Keep your footsteps soft as rain
exercises.tip: Switch to marching with one foot always grounded if jogging feels uncomfortable or unsteady.

exercises.name: Hip Openers
exercises.description: Facing the wall for support, lift one knee in front of you and circle it out to the side before lowering your foot. This controlled opening explores hip movement while your pelvis stays level and square to the wall.
steps: Stand facing the wall, feet hip-width apart, palms on the wall at shoulder height.
Shift onto your right foot and lift your left knee in front of your hip.
Circle your left knee out to the side without turning your chest or pelvis.
Lower your foot gently beside the other, then switch legs.
Alternate sides slowly, breathing freely and keeping each circle smooth.
exercises.breath: Exhale to open, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Open a gate with your knee
exercises.tip: Lift your knee only as high as you can without leaning or twisting.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: Use the wall for support as you reach one arm upward and extend the opposite leg behind you. This standing variation challenges cross-body coordination while you keep your spine and pelvis steady.
steps: Stand facing the wall, placing both palms at shoulder height.
Step back slightly and gently firm your middle, keeping knees soft.
Slide your right hand upward and reach your left leg behind you.
Lift your left foot slightly, keeping your hips level and back long.
Exhale to return, then alternate sides with slow, comfortable reaches.
exercises.breath: Inhale to reach, exhale to return
exercises.cue: Reach long without tipping your tray
exercises.tip: Keep your back toes on the floor if lifting your foot makes your lower back arch.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Wall Bridge Left
exercises.description: Extend your right leg toward the ceiling and lift your hips by pressing only through your left foot on the wall. Working one side at a time strengthens the glutes and keeps the pelvis honest.
steps: Lie on your back with both soles on the wall.
Straighten your right leg up toward the ceiling.
Press through your left foot and lift your hips, pelvis level.
Lower with control and lift again.
exercises.breath: Exhale up, inhale down
exercises.cue: Lift from the standing foot
exercises.tip: Keep both feet on the wall if your pelvis tilts or your foot slips.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Wall Bridge Right
exercises.description: Extend your left leg toward the ceiling and lift your hips by pressing only through your right foot on the wall. Working one side at a time strengthens the glutes and keeps the pelvis honest.
steps: Lie on your back with both soles on the wall.
Straighten your left leg up toward the ceiling.
Press through your right foot and lift your hips, pelvis level.
Lower with control and lift again.
exercises.breath: Exhale up, inhale down
exercises.cue: Lift from the standing foot
exercises.tip: Use a small lift, and return both feet to the wall whenever you need support.

exercises.name: Wall Bridge
exercises.description: Lie with your feet flat on the wall and peel your hips up into a long bridge, then roll down slowly. Pressing through the wall works your glutes and the backs of your thighs while your spine moves bone by bone.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, soles flat on the wall.
Rest your arms beside you and press your feet into the wall.
Peel your hips up until ribs, hips and knees form one line.
Roll your spine slowly back down to the mat and repeat.
exercises.breath: Exhale to lift, inhale to lower
exercises.cue: Peel up, roll down bone by bone
exercises.tip: Keep the knee opening small enough that your feet stay secure against the wall.

exercises.name: Crossbody Toe Touch
exercises.description: Reach one hand toward your opposite toes as you curl your upper back from the floor. With your feet supported by the wall, this diagonal reach strengthens your abdominal muscles and develops crossbody coordination.
steps: Lie on your back with both feet supported against the wall.
Keep your knees softly bent and reach your arms forward.
Curl your shoulders up, reaching your right hand toward your left toes.
Lower gently, then reach your left hand toward your right toes.
Alternate sides slowly, exhaling to reach and inhaling to lower.
exercises.breath: Exhale to reach, inhale to lower
exercises.cue: Reach along a gentle diagonal
exercises.tip: Reach toward your shin instead of your toes, and avoid pulling your chin forward.

exercises.name: Marching Wall Bridge
exercises.description: Hold a bridge with your feet on the wall and lift one foot at a time without letting your hips drop. The slow march builds glute strength and deep core control.
steps: Lie on your back with soles on the wall and arms beside you.
Press into the wall and lift your hips into a bridge.
Keeping hips level, lift your right foot slightly off the wall.
Replace it, then lift your left foot, marching slowly.
Lower your hips with control when you finish.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly while you march
exercises.cue: Hips high and level like a table
exercises.tip: Stop lifting before your back arches, and keep pressure away from your neck.

exercises.name: Lower Abs Crunch
exercises.description: With your feet resting against the wall, curl your shoulders up and reach your hands forward. The supported leg position lets you focus on abdominal strength without swinging your legs for momentum.
steps: Lie on your back with feet against the wall, knees over hips.
Bend your knees to right angles and reach your arms forward.
Exhale and curl your shoulder blades slightly off the floor.
Reach toward the wall, keeping your legs still and neck long.
Inhale as you lower, then repeat with a small, smooth curl.
exercises.breath: Exhale to curl, inhale to lower
exercises.cue: Slide your ribs toward your hips
exercises.tip: You do not need to touch the wall; keep your neck comfortable throughout.

exercises.name: Knee to Chest Left
exercises.description: With both feet on the wall, lift your left foot away and hug that knee in toward your chest. The quiet hold releases the left hip and lower back after strength work.
steps: Lie on your back with both feet resting on the wall.
Lift your left foot away and hold behind or over your left knee.
Draw the knee gently toward your chest, right foot on the wall.
Breathe into the stretch, then return the foot to the wall.
exercises.breath: Long, slow breaths into the belly
exercises.cue: Hug the knee, soften the back
exercises.tip: Bend your right knee and plant that foot if keeping the leg straight feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Knee to Chest Right
exercises.description: With both feet on the wall, lift your right foot away and hug that knee in toward your chest. The quiet hold releases the right hip and lower back after strength work.
steps: Lie on your back with both feet resting on the wall.
Lift your right foot away and hold behind or over your right knee.
Draw the knee gently toward your chest, left foot on the wall.
Breathe into the stretch, then return the foot to the wall.
exercises.breath: Long, slow breaths into the belly
exercises.cue: Hug the knee, soften the back
exercises.tip: Hold behind your thigh rather than pulling directly on your kneecap.

exercises.name: Supine Twist Right
exercises.description: With your arms open wide, let both bent knees lower slowly to the right while your shoulders stay grounded. The supported twist releases the lower back and outer hips.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet on the wall, arms wide.
Bring your feet together and lower both knees to the right.
Let your head turn gently to the left, shoulders heavy.
Hold for a few breaths, then draw the knees back to center.
exercises.breath: Exhale to sink deeper
exercises.cue: Knees fall, shoulders stay
exercises.tip: Keep your gaze upward if turning your head feels uncomfortable for your neck.

exercises.name: Supine Twist Left
exercises.description: With your arms open wide, let both bent knees lower slowly to the left while your shoulders stay grounded. The supported twist releases the lower back and outer hips.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet on the wall, arms wide.
Bring your feet together and lower both knees to the left.
Let your head turn gently to the right, shoulders heavy.
Hold for a few breaths, then draw the knees back to center.
exercises.breath: Exhale to sink deeper
exercises.cue: Knees fall, shoulders stay
exercises.tip: Let your knee hover rather than forcing it down toward the floor.

exercises.name: Wall Knee Pushups
exercises.description: Keep your knees grounded and your feet against the wall as you lower and press your chest away from the floor. This supported pushup strengthens your chest and arms while challenging trunk control.
steps: Kneel on the floor facing away from the wall, feet touching it.
Walk your hands forward, placing them slightly wider than your shoulders.
Align your shoulders, hips, and knees in one long line.
Bend your elbows diagonally back, lowering your chest between your hands.
Exhale as you press upward, then repeat with a controlled descent.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lower, exhale to press
exercises.cue: Move as one long, steady board
exercises.tip: Cushion your knees with a folded mat and lower only as far as comfortable.

exercises.name: Wall Plank Dips
exercises.description: From a floor plank with your feet braced against the wall, lift your hips into an inverted V and lower back to plank. This transition builds shoulder endurance and controlled abdominal support.
steps: Start on all fours, facing away from the wall with hands beneath shoulders.
Extend your legs into plank, bracing your toes at the wall base.
Press through your hands and lift your hips into an inverted V.
Lower your hips to shoulder height, keeping arms straight and gaze down.
Exhale into plank, then inhale as you lift your hips again.
exercises.breath: Inhale hips up, exhale into plank
exercises.cue: Lift a tent, return to plank
exercises.tip: Avoid dropping your hips below plank height, and rest your knees whenever needed.

exercises.name: Squat to Calf Raises
exercises.description: With your hands resting on the wall, bend into a shallow squat, stand tall, and lift your heels. This sequence builds leg strength and ankle control for steadier everyday movement.
steps: Stand facing the wall, feet shoulder-width apart, hands at chest height.
Bend your knees and send your hips back into a shallow squat.
Press through your feet to straighten your legs without locking knees.
Lift both heels, keeping your weight balanced across your toes.
Lower your heels slowly, then repeat the sequence with steady breaths.
exercises.breath: Exhale to stand, inhale to lower
exercises.cue: Rise like a gentle elevator
exercises.tip: Use the wall for balance, and keep your squat shallow if your knees feel uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Wall Supported Push Ups
exercises.description: Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, then press yourself away with steady palms. You strengthen your chest and arms while practicing firm, aligned support through your trunk.
steps: Stand facing the wall, placing your palms at shoulder height.
Step your feet back, keeping your body aligned from head to heels.
Bend your elbows diagonally back as your chest approaches the wall.
Exhale and press through your palms to straighten your arms.
Repeat slowly, inhaling toward the wall and exhaling away.
exercises.breath: Inhale toward the wall, exhale away
exercises.cue: Move as one long line
exercises.tip: Step closer to the wall for less effort, and keep your shoulders away from your ears.

exercises.name: Wall Chest Stretch Left
exercises.description: Rest your left palm on the wall at shoulder height and slowly turn your body away. This supported stretch gives the front of your left shoulder and chest more room to lengthen.
steps: Stand side-on to the wall with your left side closest to it.
Place your left palm on the wall at shoulder height, arm long and elbow soft.
Turn your feet and chest slowly toward the right, keeping your palm in place.
Pause at a mild stretch across your left chest, breathing slowly.
exercises.breath: Exhale into the turn, then breathe gently
exercises.cue: Open your chest like a book
exercises.tip: Turn only until you feel a gentle stretch, not pulling in the shoulder joint.

exercises.name: Wall Chest Stretch Right
exercises.description: Rest your right palm on the wall at shoulder height and slowly turn your body away. This supported stretch gives the front of your right shoulder and chest more room to lengthen.
steps: Stand side-on to the wall with your right side closest to it.
Place your right palm on the wall at shoulder height, arm long and elbow soft.
Turn your feet and chest slowly toward the left, keeping your palm in place.
Pause at a mild stretch across your right chest, breathing slowly.
exercises.breath: Exhale into the turn, then breathe gently
exercises.cue: Open your chest like a book
exercises.tip: Turn only until you feel a gentle stretch, not pulling in the shoulder joint.

exercises.name: Wall Side Stretch Left
exercises.description: Place your left hand on the wall and arc your right arm overhead as you lean left. This supported side bend lengthens your right waist and encourages comfortable sideways movement.
steps: Stand with your left side beside the wall, feet comfortably wide.
Place your left palm on the wall at shoulder height.
Reach your right arm overhead and gently bend toward the wall.
Keep both feet grounded and your chest facing forward.
Breathe into your right ribs, then return upright and repeat slowly.
exercises.breath: Inhale upright, exhale into the bend
exercises.cue: Make a rainbow with your arm
exercises.tip: Rest your right hand on your hip if reaching overhead feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Wall Side Stretch Right
exercises.description: Place your right hand on the wall and arc your left arm overhead as you lean right. This supported side bend lengthens your left waist and encourages comfortable sideways movement.
steps: Stand with your right side beside the wall, feet comfortably wide.
Place your right palm on the wall at shoulder height.
Reach your left arm overhead and gently bend toward the wall.
Keep both feet grounded and your chest facing forward.
Breathe into your left ribs, then return upright and repeat slowly.
exercises.breath: Inhale upright, exhale into the bend
exercises.cue: Make a rainbow with your arm
exercises.tip: Rest your left hand on your hip if reaching overhead feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Wall Arm Angels
exercises.description: Slide your bent arms upward and downward with your back resting against the wall. This movement develops shoulder control and helps you practice overhead reaching without arching your lower back.
steps: Stand with your back against the wall, feet slightly forward.
Soften your knees and keep your ribs comfortably settled.
Bend your elbows, bringing your arms into a wide goalpost shape.
Slide your arms upward only as far as your ribs stay quiet.
Lower slowly, exhaling upward and inhaling as your arms return.
exercises.breath: Exhale upward, inhale as you lower
exercises.cue: Let your arms glide on rails
exercises.tip: Let your hands hover away from the wall rather than forcing contact or arching your back.

exercises.name: Wall Arm Butterflies
exercises.description: Open your bent arms from in front of your chest toward the wall behind you. This gentle butterfly motion engages your upper back and gives the front of your shoulders room to lengthen.
steps: Stand with your back against the wall, feet slightly forward.
Soften your knees and raise bent arms in front of your chest.
Open your elbows outward toward the wall, keeping shoulders relaxed.
Bring your forearms together again without rounding away from the wall.
Repeat gently, exhaling to open and inhaling as your arms close.
exercises.breath: Exhale to open, inhale to close
exercises.cue: Open your arms like soft wings
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows below shoulder height if needed, and do not force them against the wall.

exercises.name: Wall Shoulder Taps
exercises.description: Lean into a wall plank and alternate tapping each shoulder with your opposite hand. You build shoulder support and trunk control as you keep your body steady.
steps: Stand facing the wall with your feet hip-width apart.
Place palms at shoulder height, then step back into a gentle lean.
Press through your left palm and tap your left shoulder with your right hand.
Return your right palm, then tap your right shoulder with your left hand.
Alternate slowly, keeping your hips quiet and breathing evenly.
exercises.breath: Exhale to tap, inhale to return
exercises.cue: Keep your hips like still water
exercises.tip: Step closer to the wall if your hips sway or your wrists feel strained.

exercises.name: Marching in Place
exercises.description: Face the wall with your hands resting on it and alternate lifting your knees in a steady march. You practice controlled weight shifts and leg coordination while keeping your upper body tall.
steps: Stand facing the wall, feet hip-width apart, palms resting at chest height.
Shift onto your left foot and lift your right knee comfortably.
Lower your right foot gently, then lift your left knee.
Continue alternating at an easy pace, breathing steadily and landing softly.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly with your marching rhythm
exercises.cue: March tall, land like a feather
exercises.tip: Lift each foot just above the floor if higher knees make you lean backward.

exercises.name: Wall Side Leg Swings Right
exercises.description: Rest both hands on the wall and swing your right leg gently sideways, then across your body. This encourages hip mobility while your standing leg and trunk practice keeping you steady.
steps: Stand facing the wall, feet hip-width apart, with both palms supported.
Shift onto your left leg and soften your standing knee.
Lift your right foot and swing it gently out to the right.
Guide your right leg back across your body without twisting your hips.
Repeat in a small, smooth arc while breathing comfortably.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly through each gentle swing
exercises.cue: Let your leg trace a gentle arc
exercises.tip: Keep your swings low and controlled rather than using momentum to reach farther.

exercises.name: Wall Side Leg Swings Left
exercises.description: Rest both hands on the wall and swing your left leg gently sideways, then across your body. This encourages hip mobility while your standing leg and trunk practice keeping you steady.
steps: Stand facing the wall, feet hip-width apart, with both palms supported.
Shift onto your right leg and soften your standing knee.
Lift your left foot and swing it gently out to the left.
Guide your left leg back across your body without twisting your hips.
Repeat in a small, smooth arc while breathing comfortably.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly through each gentle swing
exercises.cue: Let your leg trace a gentle arc
exercises.tip: Keep your swings low and controlled rather than using momentum to reach farther.

exercises.name: Wall Plie Squats
exercises.description: With your hands resting on the wall, bend and straighten your knees in a wide, gently turned-out stance. This supported squat strengthens your thighs and hips while practicing steady knee alignment.
steps: Stand facing the wall with feet wide and toes slightly turned outward.
Place your palms against the wall and lengthen your spine.
Bend your knees toward your toes, lowering only as far as comfortable.
Press through both feet to stand tall without locking your knees.
Repeat smoothly, inhaling as you lower and exhaling as you rise.
exercises.breath: Inhale down, exhale to stand
exercises.cue: Lower as though riding an elevator
exercises.tip: Keep your heels grounded, and choose a shallow squat if your knees feel uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Wall Reverse Lunges
exercises.description: Rest your hands on the wall as you step one foot back and bend both knees. Alternating these supported lunges builds leg strength and control when shifting your weight.
steps: Stand facing the wall with your feet hip-width apart.
Place your palms on the wall at chest height.
Step your right foot back, lift that heel, and bend both knees.
Press through your left foot and bring your right foot forward.
Alternate legs slowly, exhaling as you return to standing.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lower, exhale to return
exercises.cue: Lower like a gentle elevator
exercises.tip: Keep your front knee aligned with your toes, and shorten the lunge as needed.

exercises.name: Wall Quad Stretch Right
exercises.description: Steady yourself against the wall and bring your right heel toward your seat, holding your ankle gently. This stretches the front of your right thigh while you practice supported standing balance.
steps: Stand facing the wall with your feet hip-width apart.
Place your left hand on the wall and soften your left knee.
Bend your right knee and hold your right ankle with your right hand.
Point your right knee downward and keep your ribs above your hips.
Hold with easy breaths, then release your foot slowly.
exercises.breath: Breathe slowly into your lower ribs
exercises.cue: Let your knee point toward earth
exercises.tip: If reaching your ankle feels strained, loop a strap around it rather than twisting.

exercises.name: Wall Quad Stretch Left
exercises.description: Steady yourself against the wall and bring your left heel toward your seat, holding your ankle gently. This stretches the front of your left thigh while you practice supported standing balance.
steps: Stand facing the wall with your feet hip-width apart.
Place your right hand on the wall and soften your right knee.
Bend your left knee and hold your left ankle with your left hand.
Point your left knee downward and keep your ribs above your hips.
Hold with easy breaths, then release your foot slowly.
exercises.breath: Breathe slowly into your lower ribs
exercises.cue: Let your knee point toward earth
exercises.tip: If reaching your ankle feels strained, loop a strap around it rather than twisting.

exercises.name: Wall Calf Stretch Right
exercises.description: Hands on the wall, step your right foot back and press its heel into the floor. This stretches your right calf and helps keep your ankle moving freely for confident steps.
steps: Stand facing the wall and place your palms on it at shoulder height.
Step your right foot a long stride back, toes pointing at the wall.
Bend your left knee and keep your right leg long.
Press your right heel down and lean your hips toward the wall.
Hold and breathe slowly, then step your feet back together.
exercises.breath: Exhale as you sink your heel
exercises.cue: Heel heavy, leg long
exercises.tip: If your right heel lifts, shorten your stride until it stays down.

exercises.name: Wall Calf Stretch Left
exercises.description: Hands on the wall, step your left foot back and press its heel into the floor. This stretches your left calf and helps keep your ankle moving freely for confident steps.
steps: Stand facing the wall and place your palms on it at shoulder height.
Step your left foot a long stride back, toes pointing at the wall.
Bend your right knee and keep your left leg long.
Press your left heel down and lean your hips toward the wall.
Hold and breathe slowly, then step your feet back together.
exercises.breath: Exhale as you sink your heel
exercises.cue: Heel heavy, leg long
exercises.tip: If your left heel lifts, shorten your stride until it stays down.

exercises.name: Chest Pull March
exercises.description: You march with high knees while punching your arms forward and pulling the elbows back hard. It raises your heart rate and strengthens the upper back without leaving the chair.
steps: Sit near the front of your chair with your back tall.
Start marching briskly, lifting the knees high.
Punch both arms forward at chest height.
Pull the elbows back hard and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Keep the march and the pull going in a steady rhythm.
exercises.breath: Exhale on every pull
exercises.cue: Row the boat while you run
exercises.tip: Squeeze the shoulder blades on each pull and keep the shoulders away from the ears.

exercises.name: Crossed-Arm March
exercises.description: Arms crossed over your chest, you march quickly with high knees from your chair. Without the arms helping, your core does the work and your heart rate climbs fast.
steps: Sit near the front of your chair with your back tall.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Lift your left knee high, then your right.
Keep marching quickly with your core braced.
Stay tall and keep a lively, steady pace.
exercises.breath: Breathe in rhythm with your knees
exercises.cue: Run tall from your chair
exercises.tip: Lift the knees, not the shoulders; the back stays tall the whole time.

exercises.name: Press and Leg Reach
exercises.description: You press both arms forward while straightening one leg out in front, then switch legs. It strengthens the thighs and shoulders together and keeps the heart rate up.
steps: Sit tall near the front of your chair, fists at your chest.
Press both arms straight forward.
At the same time, straighten your left leg in front.
Draw arms and leg back, then press with the right leg.
Keep alternating in a brisk, steady rhythm.
exercises.breath: Exhale as you press
exercises.cue: Press and reach at the same time
exercises.tip: Straighten the leg without locking the knee and keep your back tall.

exercises.name: Overhead Pull March
exercises.description: You march with high knees while reaching both arms overhead and pulling the elbows down to your ribs. It works the back and shoulders and gets your whole body moving.
steps: Sit near the front of your chair with your back tall.
Start a brisk march, knees lifting high.
Reach both arms straight overhead.
Pull the elbows down strongly to your ribs.
Keep reaching and pulling with every few steps.
exercises.breath: Exhale as you pull down
exercises.cue: Pull down a bar from the sky
exercises.tip: Reach long and pull with the back muscles, not just the arms.

exercises.name: Seated Cross-Body Punch
exercises.description: With fists guarding your chin, you punch across your body and rotate through the ribs, alternating sides. It works the core and shoulders and lifts your heart rate quickly.
steps: Sit tall near the front of your chair, feet wide.
Raise your fists to guard your chin.
Punch your right fist across your body to the left.
Pull it back and punch your left fist across to the right.
Keep alternating quickly and turn from the ribs.
exercises.breath: Exhale sharply with each punch
exercises.cue: Punch through and turn your ribs
exercises.tip: Rotate from the ribs, keep the hips still and never lock the elbow.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Twist
exercises.description: Hands behind your ears, you lift one knee high and twist the opposite elbow toward it, then switch. It works the waist and core and keeps your heart rate up.
steps: Sit near the front of your chair, hands behind your ears.
Lift your left knee high toward your chest.
Twist your right elbow toward that knee.
Return to centre and switch to the other side.
Keep alternating in a brisk, steady rhythm.
exercises.breath: Exhale as you twist
exercises.cue: Bring elbow and knee to meet
exercises.tip: Keep the elbows wide and turn the chest; do not pull on your neck.

exercises.name: Side Push Step
exercises.description: You step one foot wide to the side while pushing both palms strongly the same way, then switch. It works the legs, shoulders and core in a brisk side-to-side rhythm.
steps: Sit near the front of your chair with hands at your chest.
Step your left foot wide out to the side.
Push both palms strongly toward your left.
Step back in and repeat to the right.
Keep stepping and pushing side to side briskly.
exercises.breath: Exhale with every push
exercises.cue: Push the wall away to each side
exercises.tip: Step wide but stay centred on the seat; the push comes from the shoulders and core.

exercises.name: Stacked-Hand Knee Lift
exercises.description: You hold stacked hands overhead and bring them down to meet each knee as it lifts high. It works the core and raises your heart rate with a big, rhythmic motion.
steps: Sit near the front of your chair, back tall.
Stack your hands and hold them above your head.
Bring the hands down to meet your left knee as it lifts.
Reach back up, then meet your right knee.
Keep alternating quickly with a strong core.
exercises.breath: Exhale as hands meet knee
exercises.cue: Chop down to meet your knee
exercises.tip: Bring the knee up to the hands rather than rounding your back down.

exercises.name: Kick with the Right Heel
exercises.description: Cross your wrists, rise onto your left leg, lift the right knee and press slowly out through the heel as both arms open wide. Form 13 of the 24 is the course's first true balance challenge.
steps: Cross your wrists in front of your chest, right wrist outside.
Shift fully onto your left leg, knee soft.
Lift your right knee to a comfortable height.
Open both arms out to the sides as you press the right heel forward.
Hold for a breath, then fold the knee back in and lower the foot.
exercises.breath: Exhale as the heel extends
exercises.cue: Rise, open, press the heel
exercises.tip: Kick at knee height or lower while you learn; a wall or chair-back within reach is perfectly fine.

exercises.name: Turn and Kick with the Left Heel
exercises.description: The mirror of the right heel kick: turn, settle onto your right leg and press out through the left heel with both arms open. Practising both sides evens out balance and leg strength.
steps: Turn your body to the left and cross your wrists in front of your chest.
Settle your weight fully onto your right leg.
Lift your left knee to a comfortable height.
Open both arms wide as you press the left heel forward.
Hold for a breath, then fold the knee and lower the foot with control.
exercises.breath: Exhale as the heel extends
exercises.cue: Root the right foot, kick with the left
exercises.tip: Fix your eyes on one still point ahead; steady eyes make a steady standing leg.

exercises.name: Strike the Ears with Both Fists
exercises.description: Step into a bow stance as both hands drop, close into soft fists and circle up to meet in front at head height. A powerful, rounded shape that trains forward weight shift and open shoulders.
steps: Lift your right knee and lower both open hands beside it.
Step your right foot forward, heel first.
Shift forward into a bow stance as your hands drop beside your hips.
Close the hands into loose fists and circle them outward and up.
Bring the fists toward each other at head height, arms rounded.
exercises.breath: Exhale as the fists rise and meet
exercises.cue: Circle wide, meet in front
exercises.tip: Keep the fists loose and the elbows slightly down so the shape stays round, never tense.

exercises.name: Golden Rooster Stands on One Leg
exercises.description: Rise out of Snake Creeps Down onto one leg, lifting the other knee as the same-side hand rises in front. It is the classic Tai Chi balance posture, and a direct workout for the muscles that prevent falls.
steps: Shift your weight forward onto your left leg.
Rise up as your right knee lifts to hip height or lower.
Let your right hand rise in front, fingers up, elbow above the knee.
Press your left hand down beside your left hip.
Hold steady for a breath, then lower the foot and change sides.
exercises.breath: Inhale as you rise · breathe softly while you hold
exercises.cue: Rise tall like a rooster
exercises.tip: Lift the knee only as high as you can hold steadily; a low, calm lift beats a high, wobbly one.

exercises.name: Needle at Sea Bottom
exercises.description: Sit back onto your right leg, touch the left toes forward and hinge from the hips as your right fingertips reach down toward the floor. A gentle forward fold with a long spine that stretches the legs and back.
steps: Shift your weight back onto your right leg.
Draw your left foot in, only the ball of the foot touching down.
Lift your right hand up beside your right ear.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long back as the fingertips point down ahead.
Let your left hand rest by your left thigh, then rise slowly.
exercises.breath: Exhale as you hinge · inhale as you rise
exercises.cue: Hinge long, point deep
exercises.tip: Hinge only as far as your back stays long; bend the standing knee more rather than rounding.

exercises.name: Fan Through Back
exercises.description: Step forward into a bow stance as your arms open like a fan, one palm pushing ahead while the other rises beside your temple. The form opens the upper back and chest and links the needle to the final section.
steps: Rise from the needle and lift both hands in front of your chest.
Step your left foot forward, heel first.
Shift forward into a bow stance, front knee over the ankle.
Push your left palm forward at nose height.
Raise your right hand beside your right temple, palm turned out.
exercises.breath: Exhale as the arms open
exercises.cue: Open the fan through your back
exercises.tip: Feel the stretch spread across your shoulder blades rather than forcing the arms wider.

exercises.name: Deflect, Parry and Punch
exercises.description: Roll your fist down and out to deflect, sweep the other palm forward to parry, then step and punch slowly straight ahead. Three linked actions that train coordination, rotation and a strong, rooted stance.
steps: Form a loose right fist and roll it down and out in front of you.
Step your left foot forward as the left palm sweeps ahead to parry.
Draw the right fist back beside your waist, palm up.
Shift into a bow stance and punch the right fist straight forward.
Keep the thumb on top and the left palm resting near the right forearm.
exercises.breath: Exhale with the punch
exercises.cue: Deflect, parry, punch
exercises.tip: The punch comes from the legs and waist; keep the elbow slightly bent and never snap the arm straight.

exercises.name: Withdraw and Push
exercises.description: Sit back and draw both hands toward your chest, then shift forward and push both palms out. Also called Apparent Close-Up, it teaches the essential Tai Chi rhythm of yielding and returning.
steps: Reach both hands forward, palms up, in a forward stance.
Sit back into your rear leg as you draw your hands toward your chest.
Turn the palms to face forward, elbows low.
Shift forward into a bow stance and push both palms out at shoulder height.
Keep the push soft and the shoulders down.
exercises.breath: Inhale as you withdraw · exhale as you push
exercises.cue: Yield back, return forward
exercises.tip: Move the hands by moving the body; the arms stay almost still while the legs carry you back and forward.

exercises.name: Cross Hands
exercises.description: Open both arms wide in a large circle, sink gently, and gather them so the wrists cross in front of your chest. The second-to-last form gathers the whole sequence into one calm, rounded shape.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft.
Open both arms out to the sides in a wide circle.
Sink a little as the arms sweep down and inward.
Cross the wrists in front of your chest, right wrist outside.
Rise slightly and hold the round shape, as if hugging a tree.
exercises.breath: Inhale as the arms open · exhale as they gather
exercises.cue: Open wide, gather in
exercises.tip: Keep space between your arms and chest, as if holding a large balloon.

exercises.name: Closing Form
exercises.description: Turn the palms down, separate the hands, and let them float down to your sides as you stand up tall and bring the feet together. Every Tai Chi practice ends here, letting the energy of the form settle.
steps: From crossed wrists, turn both palms to face down.
Separate the hands to shoulder width in front of you.
Slowly lower the hands to your sides as your knees straighten.
Bring your left foot in beside your right foot.
Stand quietly for a few breaths and notice how you feel.
exercises.breath: One long exhale as the hands lower
exercises.cue: Float down and settle
exercises.tip: Take your time here; a slow finish helps the calm of the practice stay with you.

exercises.name: Rolling Arms
exercises.description: Turn gently through your waist as one arm circles back and the other presses forward. This alternating flow encourages comfortable shoulder movement and coordination between your arms and torso.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft and arms relaxed.
Turn your waist gently right, sweeping your right arm back and upward.
Bend your right elbow, bringing your hand beside your ear.
Press your right palm forward as your left arm circles back.
Alternate sides slowly, letting your waist turn with each sweep.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly through each rolling sweep
exercises.cue: Let your arms roll like waves
exercises.tip: Keep each backward sweep small enough that your shoulder stays comfortable and relaxed.

exercises.name: Scooping the Sea and Looking at the Sky
exercises.description: Reach low with crossed wrists, then rise and spread your arms toward the sky. Moving between these levels builds awareness of your weight shift and encourages coordinated leg and arm movement.
steps: Stand with one foot forward, feet comfortably apart for balance.
Bend your front knee and hinge slightly forward, crossing your wrists low.
Press through your feet to rise, uncrossing and lifting your arms.
Open your arms overhead comfortably, letting your gaze follow without tipping back.
Exhale as you scoop low, then inhale as you open.
exercises.breath: Exhale to scoop, inhale to open
exercises.cue: Gather water, open to the sky
exercises.tip: Keep your scoop shallow and look forward if looking upward feels unsteady.

exercises.name: Flying Dove Spreads Its Wings
exercises.description: Rock gently between your feet as your arms open like wings and gather forward again. This flowing exchange builds awareness of your weight shifts while linking shoulder movement with breath.
steps: Stand with one foot forward, feet comfortably apart, and knees soft.
Reach both arms forward at chest height, palms gently touching.
Shift your weight backward and open your arms comfortably wide.
Shift forward again, bringing your palms together without locking your elbows.
Inhale as you open, then exhale as you gather.
exercises.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to gather
exercises.cue: Spread your wings, then gather
exercises.tip: Keep both feet grounded and shorten your stance if you feel unsteady.

exercises.name: Flying Wild Goose
exercises.description: Float your arms outward as your heels lift, then lower into a shallow knee bend. This gentle rise and fall challenges your balance while engaging your calves and coordinating your whole body.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms resting by your sides.
Float your arms out sideways as you lift your heels slightly.
Lower your arms and heels together, bending your knees into a shallow squat.
Inhale as you rise, then exhale as you settle.
exercises.breath: Inhale to rise, exhale to settle
exercises.cue: Spread your wings, settle softly
exercises.tip: Keep your heels grounded if lifting them makes you feel unsteady.

exercises.name: Spinning Wheel
exercises.description: Sweep your arms in a broad circle, traveling down one side, across your legs, and overhead. The continuous arc encourages comfortable trunk mobility and coordinated weight shifts through your feet.
steps: Stand with your feet wide and your knees comfortably bent.
Soften your hips and sweep both arms down beside one leg.
Circle your hands across your shins, bending only as far as comfortable.
Rise through your legs, sweeping both arms up the other side and overhead.
Continue circling slowly, breathing evenly and shifting your weight smoothly.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly throughout each circle
exercises.cue: Trace a great wheel through air
exercises.tip: Make the circle smaller and keep your hands above your knees if bending feels uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Stepping and Bouncing the Ball
exercises.description: Lift one knee and the hand on that side, then lower them as though gently bouncing a ball. Alternating sides develops stepping coordination and balance as you transfer your weight.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed.
Shift onto your left foot, lifting your right knee and right hand.
If steady, lift your left heel slightly while keeping your gaze forward.
Lower your heel and right foot, gently pressing your right palm downward.
Repeat on the other side, alternating slowly with easy breaths.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to lower
exercises.cue: Bounce an imaginary ball softly
exercises.tip: Keep your supporting heel down and lift each foot just slightly for an easier version.

exercises.name: Pressing Palms to Calm the Qi
exercises.description: Lift your upturned palms to your chest, then turn them downward and sink gently through your knees. Matching this simple arm pattern with your breath encourages relaxed shoulders and a steady movement rhythm.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft and hands near your hips.
Turn your palms upward and inhale, lifting your hands to chest height.
Turn your palms downward, keeping your elbows relaxed beside your ribs.
Exhale and press toward your hips while gently bending your knees.
Repeat smoothly, letting each breath guide the lift and lowering.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to press
exercises.cue: Press gently through still water
exercises.tip: Use a small knee bend and keep your weight spread across both feet.

exercises.name: Two Hands Hold Up the Heavens
exercises.description: Lace your fingers near your belly, lift your hands, and turn your palms toward the ceiling. This upward reach encourages shoulder mobility and a gentle lengthening through the sides of your torso.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and fingers loosely interlaced near your belly.
Lift your joined hands past your chest and toward your face.
Turn your palms upward and reach overhead without locking your elbows.
Release your fingers and float your arms down by your sides.
Repeat slowly, inhaling to reach and exhaling to lower.
exercises.breath: Inhale to reach, exhale to lower
exercises.cue: Lift the sky with soft hands
exercises.tip: Reach only as high as comfortable, keeping your ribs from flaring forward.

exercises.name: Drawing the Bow Left
exercises.description: Settle into a wide stance and extend your left hand as your right elbow draws back. This bow-shaped action engages your upper back while your legs support a steady, grounded position.
steps: Stand with feet wide, knees softly bent and wrists crossed at chest height.
Extend your left hand leftward, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Draw your right hand toward your right shoulder, leading with your elbow.
Look toward your left hand while keeping your torso facing forward.
Exhale to return your wrists to center, then repeat slowly.
exercises.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to return
exercises.cue: Draw a bow with quiet strength
exercises.tip: Keep your knees aligned with your toes and make the stance narrower if needed.

exercises.name: Drawing the Bow Right
exercises.description: Settle into a wide stance and extend your right hand as your left elbow draws back. This deliberate opening engages your upper back and helps you coordinate your arms without shifting your grounded stance.
steps: Stand with feet wide, knees softly bent and wrists crossed at chest height.
Extend your right hand rightward, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Draw your left hand toward your left shoulder, leading with your elbow.
Look toward your right hand while keeping your torso facing forward.
Exhale to return your wrists to center, then repeat slowly.
exercises.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to return
exercises.cue: Open the bow, anchor your feet
exercises.tip: Let your shoulders stay low, and avoid pulling your elbow behind your torso.

exercises.name: Separate Heaven and Earth
exercises.description: Reach one palm overhead while the other presses toward the floor, then exchange sides through your center. These opposing reaches encourage gentle torso length and help your shoulders move independently.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands resting in front of your belly.
Lift your right hand overhead, turning your palm toward the ceiling.
Press your left palm toward the floor beside your left hip.
Return both hands to your belly, then switch the reaching arms.
Inhale as your hands separate, and exhale as they return.
exercises.breath: Inhale to separate, exhale to return
exercises.cue: Create space between earth and sky
exercises.tip: Keep your torso upright and shorten the overhead reach if your shoulder feels strained.

exercises.name: Wise Owl Gazes Backward
exercises.description: Stand tall with open palms as you slowly turn your head and shoulders to look behind you. This gentle rotation encourages upper-back mobility and steady balance over grounded feet.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees comfortably soft.
Turn your palms forward and let your shoulders settle.
Slowly turn your head and shoulders right, keeping hips facing forward.
Return to center, then turn left within a comfortable range.
Continue alternating sides slowly, breathing easily through each turn.
exercises.breath: Exhale to turn, inhale to center
exercises.cue: Look back like a watchful owl
exercises.tip: Let your gaze follow the turn without forcing your chin toward your shoulder.

exercises.name: Sway the Head and Shake the Tail
exercises.description: Settle into a wide stance and sweep your torso through a gentle arc as your hips sway. You practice smooth weight shifts while building comfortable movement through your hips and trunk.
steps: Stand with feet wide, knees softly bent, and hands on thighs.
Hinge slightly forward, keeping your neck aligned with your back.
Shift toward your right leg as your torso follows.
Sweep your torso gently through center toward your left leg.
Continue swaying side to side with an easy, unhurried breath.
exercises.breath: Breathe evenly through each gentle sway
exercises.cue: Sway like a reed in water
exercises.tip: Keep the stance shallow and let your knees follow the direction of your toes.

exercises.name: Two Hands Hold the Feet
exercises.description: Reach your arms upward, then fold gently and slide your hands down your legs toward your feet. This flowing reach and fold explores shoulder mobility and lengthens the backs of your legs.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Lift your arms overhead only as far as feels comfortable.
Hinge at your hips, sliding your hands down your legs.
Pause at a comfortable height, keeping your knees soft.
Slowly return upright, then inhale as you reach upward again.
exercises.breath: Exhale to fold, inhale to rise
exercises.cue: Fold like a soft ribbon
exercises.tip: Rest your hands on your thighs or shins instead of reaching for your feet.

exercises.name: Clench the Fists with Angry Eyes
exercises.description: From a wide, shallow stance, extend one fist slowly forward, then open your hand and draw it back. You coordinate deliberate arm movements with a steady lower body and focused gaze.
steps: Stand with feet wide, knees softly bent, and fists beside waist.
Extend your right fist forward slowly, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Focus your gaze ahead while relaxing your jaw and shoulders.
Open your right hand, gently close it, and draw it back.
Alternate arms, exhaling forward and inhaling back toward your waist.
exercises.breath: Exhale forward, inhale as you return
exercises.cue: Send your fist through thick water
exercises.tip: Keep your fists lightly closed and avoid locking your elbows as you reach.

exercises.name: Bouncing on the Toes
exercises.description: Lift your heels to balance on the balls of your feet, then settle them softly onto the floor. You strengthen your calves and practice controlling small changes in your standing balance.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed beside you.
Press through the balls of your feet to lift your heels.
Pause briefly at a height where you feel steady.
Lower your heels softly, letting your knees absorb the landing.
Repeat small rises and soft landings with an easy breath.
exercises.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to settle
exercises.cue: Rise lightly, land like a feather
exercises.tip: Keep your heels close to the floor if a higher lift feels unsteady.

exercises.name: Cloud Steps
exercises.description: Glide sideways on softly bent knees while your hands float across your view in alternating arcs. You build controlled lateral steps and coordinate your arms with smooth changes of weight.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and hands before chest.
Shift onto your left leg, then step right with toes first.
Settle your right heel and shift your weight onto that foot.
Draw your left foot inward as your hands float across your view.
Continue sideways slowly, then reverse direction while keeping your height steady.
exercises.breath: Breathe smoothly as you shift and step
exercises.cue: Glide beneath a low ceiling
exercises.tip: Take small steps and keep your feet apart rather than bringing them together.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.description: Rest your back against a wall and slide into a supported squat, holding at a comfortable depth. You build endurance through your thighs while practicing steady trunk control and relaxed breathing.
steps: Stand with your back against a wall, feet hip-width apart.
Walk your feet forward, keeping your back supported by the wall.
Slide down slightly, bending your knees while keeping heels grounded.
Keep your knees aligned over your ankles and shoulders relaxed.
Hold while breathing steadily, then press through your feet to rise.
exercises.breath: Breathe steadily without holding your breath
exercises.cue: Let the wall hold your back
exercises.tip: Stay higher on the wall if your knees feel uncomfortable or your breathing becomes strained.

plans.title: Morning Energy Boost
plans.subtitle: 10 min · Qigong & Tai Chi wake-up
plans.description: Shake loose, open the chest, paint the rainbow and lift the heavens, then step through three Tai Chi forms and finish bouncing on the toes. A standing wake-up that leaves you warm, loose and clear.

plans.title: Evening Relax Stretch
plans.subtitle: 7 min · unwind before sleep
plans.description: Standing twists, side bends and long hip, thigh and shoulder stretches, finished with slow belly breathing to let the day go.

plans.title: Desk Break Routine
plans.subtitle: 5 min · stand and reset
plans.description: Step away from the screen for standing Qigong: swing the stiffness out, open the chest, lengthen the sides, tap the lower back and clear your head in five minutes.

plans.title: Gentle Start Walk
plans.subtitle: 10 min · ease into movement
plans.description: An easy indoor walk — marching, heel pedals, step touches, side steps and rolling arms — finished with calf and shoulder stretches.

plans.title: Cardio Boost Walk
plans.subtitle: 15 min · arms up, heart up
plans.description: A brisk indoor walk with arms-up side taps, high-knee side taps, overhead hooks, high knees and a grapevine, cooled down with standing stretches.

plans.title: Balance & Stability Walk
plans.subtitle: 12 min · Tai Chi steps
plans.description: Tai Chi stance and weight shifts, sitting steps, the forward walk, cat steps, walking backward and cloud steps, finished on one leg.

plans.title: Fat-Burn Intervals
plans.subtitle: 20 min · the longest indoor walk
plans.description: High knees and hamstring-curl combos alternate with easier steps for twenty minutes of low-impact intervals, then a full stretch.

plans.title: Recovery Cool-Down
plans.subtitle: 10 min · stretch it out
plans.description: Slow marching into standing twists, side bends and long leg and shoulder stretches, with a quiet breath to finish.

plans.title: Chair Strength
plans.subtitle: 12 min · tone from your seat
plans.description: Seated marching, rows, curls, knee extensions, hip openers and shoulder work for real strength without standing.

plans.title: Gentle Flexibility Flow
plans.subtitle: 10 min · seated stretch
plans.description: Seated waist circles, shoulder rolls, cat-cow, side bends, a spinal twist, a chest opener and hamstring stretches from your chair.

plans.title: 7-Day Full-Body Fusion
plans.subtitle: 7 days · five styles, one week
plans.description: Try everything TaiChi Flow teaches in a single week: Tai Chi, walking cardio, Wall Pilates, Shibashi, intervals, a wall core day and the Eight Brocades. Find the style you love, then follow its full course.

plans.title: Tai Chi Foundations
plans.subtitle: 21 days · learn the classic 24-form
plans.description: Learn the Yang-style 24-form — the Tai Chi sequence practised in parks around the world — one or two postures a day. Every lesson warms you up, reviews yesterday, teaches the new form slowly, then links everything you know into one flow. Weekly sections build to day 21, when you move through all 24 forms on your own.

days.title: Strike the Ears & the left heel kick
Needle at Sea Bottom & Fan Through Back

plans.title: Chair Yoga Weight Loss
plans.subtitle: 30 days · low-impact seated burn & tone
plans.description: Seated cardio marches, cross-body punches and knee twists, plus strength, core, mobility, upper-body and leg days in rotation, all from a sturdy chair. Work blocks lengthen each week and a second round is added, with a gentle stretch day every seventh day.

plans.title: Seated Tai Chi
plans.subtitle: 28 days · 14 forms from your chair
plans.description: Fourteen seated Tai Chi and Qigong forms in three teaching weeks — seated Tai Chi, chair Qigong, then the flowing arm forms like Phoenix Wings and Catch the Moon — linked into one complete seated flow you practise in week four. Ideal for limited mobility, office days or recovery.

days.title: Waving Your Hands to the Sea

plans.title: Daily Tai Chi
plans.subtitle: 28 days · balance, strength & flow
plans.description: A daily practice in four themed weeks: rooting, balance, strength and flow. Each day pairs a short skill drill — weight shifts, one-leg balance, low stances — with Tai Chi forms that use it, and the last week links the full 24-form. Best after Tai Chi Foundations, friendly from day one.

plans.title: 30-Day Weight Loss Walking
plans.subtitle: 30 days · indoor walks from 12 to 23 minutes
plans.description: Indoor walking workouts with a new focus every day — arms-up cardio, knee drive, side steps, cross-body core, intervals and steady endurance, with dance-style side taps and cross-back steps. Work blocks grow longer each week and a Round 2 is added, with an easy recovery walk every seventh day.

plans.title: Tai Chi Walking
plans.subtitle: 21 days · steps, balance & moving calm
plans.description: Learn to walk the Tai Chi way: rooted stance, sitting steps, the heel-first forward walk, cat steps, walking backward and cloud steps — then the stepping forms that use them. Every week ends with a longer walking flow and an easy recovery day.

days.title: Golden Rooster · balance on one leg

plans.title: Balance & Breath Flow
plans.subtitle: 12 min · steady on one leg
plans.description: Hip circles and weight shifts into White Crane, Golden Rooster and Repulse the Monkey, then Cloud Hands and a long, slow breath.

plans.title: Flow & Power Basics
plans.subtitle: 12 min · rooted strength, soft hands
plans.description: Bow stances and pushing forms from the 24-form — Wild Horse’s Mane, Brush Knee, Grasp the Bird’s Tail, Single Whip and Withdraw and Push.

plans.title: Chair Qigong
plans.subtitle: 14 min · seated energy flow
plans.description: Seated breathing and the opening form, then chest openings, Lifting the Qi, Phoenix Wings, the rainbow, Catch the Moon and Washing the Face with Qi, all from your chair.

plans.title: Daily Qi Awakening
plans.subtitle: 15 min · the first nine Shibashi forms
plans.description: The opening half of Shibashi — chest openings, the rainbow, rolling arms, rowing the boat and turning to the moon — closed with stillness.

plans.title: Neck & Shoulder Release
plans.subtitle: 10 min · seated relief
plans.description: Slow neck movements in every direction, shoulder rolls and extensions, and a chest opener to undo screen posture.

plans.title: 7-Day Step & Stretch
plans.subtitle: 7 days · ease back into moving
plans.description: Seven short days of easy indoor walking steps, each finished with full-body standing stretches. A gentle way to build the habit before a longer course.

plans.title: Shibashi 18
plans.subtitle: 18 days · one Qigong form a day
plans.description: The 18 flowing forms of Tai Chi Qigong Shibashi, one new form each day. You review yesterday’s form, learn today’s slowly, then flow through the set so far. Days 6 and 12 link everything learned so far, and on day 18 you move through all eighteen.

days.title: Lifting the Ball · the first seven, linked
Turning to Gaze at the Moon
Scooping the Sea, Looking at the Sky
Pressing Palms to Calm the Qi

plans.title: Eight Brocades
plans.subtitle: 14 days · the classic Ba Duan Jin
plans.description: Ba Duan Jin, the Eight Brocades, is a thousand-year-old Qigong set of eight stretching, twisting and strengthening forms. Learn one form every day or two, then practise the whole set with breath focus, deeper stances and two full rounds.

days.title: Standing like a tree · Hold Up the Heavens
Sway the Head and Shake the Tail
Recovery · the first six, slow and full
Clench the Fists with Angry Eyes
Graduation · the full set and stillness

plans.title: 28-Day Wall Pilates
plans.subtitle: 28 days · sculpt, strengthen & stretch
plans.description: Wall Pilates standing and on the mat with your feet on the wall: squats, lunges and wall jogging, push-ups, knee push-ups and plank dips, bridges and crunches. Six rotating focuses — legs, upper body, core, full body, lower body and balance — get longer and stronger each week, with no movement repeated inside a workout and a stretch day every seventh day.

plans.title: Wall Pilates Express
plans.subtitle: 12 min · full body at the wall
plans.description: Plié squats, wall push-ups, squat-to-calf raises, shoulder taps, reverse lunges and arm angels, finished with a chest stretch.

plans.title: Wall Core & Glutes
plans.subtitle: 14 min · on the mat, feet on the wall
plans.description: Bridges, marching bridges, single-leg bridges, crunches and cross-body reaches with your feet on the wall, then knee hugs and a spinal twist.

plans.title: Shake, Tap & Wake
plans.subtitle: 8 min · Qigong self-massage wake-up
plans.description: Shake out from the knees, drum the thighs and lower back, swing from the waist, circle the hips and lift the sky. The quickest way to go from stiff to switched on.

plans.title: Eight Brocades Daily
plans.subtitle: 12 min · the complete Ba Duan Jin
plans.description: All eight brocades in one flowing practice — from Holding Up the Heavens to Bouncing on the Toes — for a full-body stretch and calm energy.

plans.title: Chair Cardio Blast
plans.subtitle: 15 min · seated heart-rate workout
plans.description: Eight seated cardio moves back to back — chest-pull and overhead-pull marches, cross-body punches, knee twists, side pushes and press-and-reach — then a hamstring stretch. A real sweat without standing.

guides.title: The 5 principles of Tai Chi
guides.subtitle: What makes slow movement so powerful
guides.intro: Tai Chi looks simple from the outside — soft arms, slow steps, a calm face. Underneath, five quiet principles turn those movements into training for balance, strength and a settled mind.

sections.heading: 1 · Relax, don't collapse
sections.body: Song, the Chinese word for relaxed, means releasing tension you don't need while keeping the posture you do. Shoulders drop, the jaw softens, but the spine stays long. You'll feel it most in the hands: alive, never limp.

sections.heading: 2 · Root through your feet
sections.body: Imagine your weight sinking into the floor through the soles of your feet. A slight bend in the knees lets the legs do the work, which builds strength in the ankles, knees and hips — the very joints that keep us steady.

sections.heading: 3 · Move from the centre
sections.body: Every arm movement begins a moment earlier in the waist. Turning from the centre protects the lower back and links the whole body into one smooth, efficient motion.

sections.heading: 4 · Separate full and empty
sections.body: At any moment one leg carries more weight than the other. Shifting it slowly and completely is the heart of balance training — your body learns exactly where its centre is.

sections.heading: 5 · Let the breath lead
sections.body: Breathing low into the belly, in through the nose, lets the pace of the movement follow the pace of the breath. Slower breath, calmer nervous system, softer movement.

guides.title: Why slow movement builds balance
guides.subtitle: The quiet training your body loves
guides.intro: Balance isn't a fixed trait — it's a skill your brain and body practise together. Slow, deliberate movement happens to be one of the best ways to train it.

sections.heading: Your three balance sensors
sections.body: Your eyes, your inner ear and thousands of tiny sensors in your feet and joints all report where you are in space. Moving slowly gives each of them time to talk to your brain, so the whole system gets sharper.

sections.heading: Strength where it counts
sections.body: Holding a soft knee bend while shifting weight works the muscles around your ankles, knees and hips in long, gentle bursts — exactly the strength that helps you recover when you trip.

sections.heading: Confidence is part of it
sections.body: When moving feels safe and controlled, you move more. That alone keeps joints supple and muscles engaged, creating a positive loop that compounds week after week.

takeaways: Balance is trainable at any age

guides.title: Breathing 101
guides.subtitle: Three breaths to calm you in a minute
guides.intro: The breath is the only part of the nervous system you can steer on purpose. A longer exhale is a direct signal to your body that it's safe to slow down.

sections.heading: Belly breath
sections.body: Rest a hand on your belly. Breathe in through the nose and let the hand rise; breathe out and let it fall. Five slow rounds are enough to notice a shift.

sections.heading: Box breath · 4-4-4-4
sections.body: Inhale for four, hold for four, exhale for four, hold for four. The steady rhythm gives a busy mind something simple to follow. Great before a meeting or a hard conversation.

sections.heading: 4-7-8 for sleep
sections.body: Inhale quietly for four, hold for seven, and exhale slowly through the mouth for eight. Start with four rounds. If holding feels uncomfortable, shorten every count — the long exhale is what matters.

guides.title: Chair practice, done right
guides.subtitle: Set up for safe, strong seated sessions
guides.intro: A chair turns every session into a supported one — perfect for stiff joints, busy days or rebuilding confidence. A few details make it even better.

sections.heading: Pick the right chair
sections.body: Choose a sturdy chair without wheels or arms, on a non-slip floor. Your feet should rest flat with knees roughly level with your hips.

sections.heading: Sit on the front half
sections.body: Scoot forward so your back is free and your spine can lengthen. Imagine a thread lifting the crown of your head while your sit bones sink down.

sections.heading: Use it as a partner
sections.body: Holding the seat for twists and leg lifts adds stability. For standing moves, keep the chair in front of you as a steady hand-rail.

guides.title: Qi, explained simply
guides.subtitle: An old idea with a modern feel
guides.intro: Qi (pronounced chee) is often translated as energy or vitality. You don't need to believe anything mystical to benefit — think of it as the feeling of a body that's warm, loose and awake.

sections.heading: What practitioners notice
sections.body: Warmth or tingling in the hands, a looser back, deeper breaths, a quieter mind. These are the everyday signs of circulation, relaxed muscles and a calmer nervous system.

sections.heading: Why the movements repeat
sections.body: Qigong forms repeat a single gentle movement many times, in rhythm with the breath. Repetition lets you stop thinking and start feeling — which is where the calm comes from.

sections.heading: How to practise
sections.body: Stand or sit comfortably, soften your knees, and follow the breath. Small and smooth beats big and forced. Finish by resting your hands on your lower belly for three breaths.

guides.title: Build a 10-minute habit
guides.subtitle: Make practice the easiest part of your day
guides.intro: Motivation fades; habits stay. The trick is to make your practice so small and so linked to your day that skipping it feels stranger than doing it.

sections.heading: Anchor it
sections.body: Attach practice to something you already do — after your morning tea, before your lunch break, when you brush your teeth at night. Set your TaiChi Flow reminder for that moment.

sections.heading: Shrink it on hard days
sections.body: On busy or low-energy days, do just one movement or a two-minute breath. Keeping the streak alive matters more than the length of the session.

sections.heading: Notice the payoff
sections.body: After each session, take one breath and notice how you feel. Linking the practice to a good feeling is what makes the habit stick.

tips.title: Soft knees, strong legs
tips.body: Keep a gentle bend in your knees in every standing move. It protects the joints and quietly builds leg strength.

tips.title: Exhale a little longer
tips.body: Make each out-breath one count longer than the in-breath. It's the quickest way to tell your body it can relax.

tips.title: Move at the speed of breath
tips.body: If you're rushing, you've left your breath behind. Slow the movement until the two feel connected again.

tips.title: Small is still practice
tips.body: Two minutes of mindful movement on a busy day keeps the habit alive. Consistency beats intensity.

tips.title: Let the shoulders drop
tips.body: Check in now: are your shoulders near your ears? Breathe out and let them melt down your back.

tips.title: Root through all four corners
tips.body: Feel the big toe, little toe and both sides of the heel pressing evenly. Balance starts at the feet.

tips.title: Turn from the waist
tips.body: Let your arms follow your centre, not lead it. Turning from the waist keeps the lower back happy.

tips.title: Water first
tips.body: Sip a glass of water before your session. Even mild dehydration can make muscles feel tight and tired.

tips.title: Same time, same cue
tips.body: Link practice to something you already do daily — morning tea or brushing your teeth — and it becomes automatic.

tips.title: Notice, then move
tips.body: Take three breaths before you begin and simply notice how your body feels. You'll move more kindly.

tips.title: Chair as a partner
tips.body: Hold the back of a sturdy chair for any balance move. Support isn't cheating — it's how confidence grows.

tips.title: Soft gaze, steady body
tips.body: Rest your eyes on a still point ahead during balance work. A steady gaze helps a steady body.

tips.title: Warm hands, calm mind
tips.body: Rub your palms together until warm, then rest them over your eyes for three breaths. Instant reset.

tips.title: Range before reach
tips.body: Move only as far as feels smooth. Range grows naturally when the body feels safe.

tips.title: Breathe low
tips.body: Place a hand on your belly and breathe so it rises first. Low breathing is calmer breathing.

tips.title: Evening wind-down
tips.body: A slow five-minute flow before bed tells your nervous system the day is done. Try it tonight.

tips.title: Celebrate the streak
tips.body: Every session counts, however short. Notice the streak and give yourself credit — it fuels tomorrow.

tips.title: Tension check
tips.body: Unclench your jaw, soften your tongue from the roof of your mouth, relax your brow. Feel the difference?

tips.title: Walk mindfully
tips.body: On your next walk, match four steps to an in-breath and four to an out-breath. Moving meditation.

tips.title: Sit tall, not stiff
tips.body: Imagine a thread lifting the crown of your head. Length in the spine, softness everywhere else.

tips.title: Shake it out
tips.body: Thirty seconds of loose shaking through hands, arms and legs releases stiffness after sitting.

tips.title: Morning light
tips.body: Practise near a window in the morning. Daylight helps set your body clock for better sleep tonight.

tips.title: Kind effort
tips.body: Aim for about 60% effort. Tai Chi rewards ease — strain closes the body, softness opens it.

tips.title: Listen to your body
tips.body: Discomfort that feels sharp or pinching is a stop sign. Ease off, adjust, or choose the seated version.

tips.title: One breath reset
tips.body: Stressed? Inhale for four, pause, exhale for six. One breath can change the next ten minutes.

tips.title: Ankles matter
tips.body: Draw slow circles with each ankle while you wait for the kettle. Strong, mobile ankles prevent wobbles.

tips.title: Finish with stillness
tips.body: End each session with hands resting on your lower belly for three breaths. Let the benefits settle.

tips.title: Progress, not perfection
tips.body: Your form will never be perfect — nobody's is. Every repetition teaches your body something new.

tips.title: Sleep is training
tips.body: Muscles and balance improve while you rest. A regular bedtime makes your practice work harder for you.

tips.title: Share the calm
tips.body: Invite a friend or family member to practise with you. Calm is contagious — and so is consistency.
